title: On The Quantum Communication Complexity Of Total Functions
authors: Dmytro Gavinsky
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a total function with a polylogarithmic two-message quantum protocol, whereas every randomised protocol, even with arbitrarily many rounds, requires polynomial communication.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a total function that can be computed with polylogarithmic communication using a two-message quantum protocol, while any randomized protocol requires polynomial communication, showing an exponential separation between quantum and classical communication complexity.
motivation: Motivated by understanding the power of quantum communication over classical communication for total functions, potentially resolving open questions about separations.
method: The authors construct a specific total function and design a two-message quantum protocol achieving polylogarithmic communication, and prove a lower bound for randomized protocols.
result: A total function exists for which quantum communication complexity is polylogarithmic while classical randomized complexity is polynomial, establishing a strong separation.
conclusion: This result shows a significant advantage of quantum communication over classical for total functions, which may have implications for understanding communication complexity and quantum information theory.

title: Multicast Quantum Network Coding As Optimal Symmetric Universal Cloning Over A Quantum Network
authors: Go Kato, Mio Murao, Masaki Owari
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of perfectly multicasting symmetric universal clones of unknown quantum states over quantum networks with free classical communication. We construct a protocol that multicasts symmetric universal clones of input states from multiple source nodes by extending the quantum network coding protocol proposed by Kobayashi et al. We further establish a sufficient condition for perfect multicast in the single-source setting. Specifically, we show that when a single copy of a [MATH]-dimensional input state is available at the source node, where [MATH] is a sufficiently large prime power, perfect multicast of the corresponding symmetric universal clone is achievable using a small amount of entanglement shared among the target nodes. This result holds for quantum networks represented by an undirected graph [MATH], where each edge corresponds to a noiseless [MATH]-dimensional quantum channel, provided that there exists an acyclic directed graph [MATH] obtained by assigning directions to the edges of [MATH] such that the minimum cut of [MATH] is at least [MATH].
tldr: This paper constructs a protocol for multicasting symmetric universal clones over quantum networks and provides a sufficient condition for perfect multicast.
motivation: To achieve efficient multicast of quantum information (clones) over networks, extending quantum network coding techniques.
method: The authors extend the quantum network coding protocol by Kobayashi et al., sharing entanglement among target nodes and leveraging acyclic orientations of the network graph.
result: They prove perfect multicast is achievable when the input state dimension is a sufficiently large prime power and the network has an acyclic orientation with minimum cut at least that dimension.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical characterization of multicast cloning over quantum networks, demonstrating feasibility under certain graph and dimension constraints.

title: Experimental Zero-added-loss Multiplexing Bell-pair Source For Long-haul Quantum Networks
authors: Yoshiaki Tsujimoto, Daiki Ichii, Rikizo Ikuta, Mikio Fujiwara, Masahiro Takeoka, Go Kato, Kentaro Wakui
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boosting the communication rate of quantum networks is a central challenge in quantum information science. Recently, an efficient entanglement distribution scheme employing quasi-deterministic Bell-pair sources based on time-frequency multiplexing, referred to as zero-added-loss multiplexing~(ZALM), has been proposed. Its implementation, however, requires high-fidelity entanglement swapping across densely multiplexed time-frequency modes, which has remained an experimental challenge. Here we demonstrate entanglement swapping across 16 parallel frequency modes with a high average fidelity of 93.9[MATH]{\%}. Notably, polarization-entangled photon pairs in each frequency mode are spectrally single-mode using only off-the-shelf 50-GHz dense wavelength-division multiplexing~(DWDM) filters, eliminating the need for additional narrowband filtering. Furthermore, in order to fully exploit the temporal degree of freedom, the pump pulse is operated with a repetition frequency of {GHz}. By combining the frequency and time multiplexing, the total swapping rate reaches 5.38[MATH]0.17\,}, which corresponds to the ZALM Bell-pair rate of {pairs\,s^{-1}}. Our results establish the key experimental capabilities required for ZALM and demonstrate a scalable route toward practical high-rate quantum repeaters and long-haul quantum networks.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a zero-added-loss multiplexing (ZALM) Bell-pair source using frequency and time multiplexing with entanglement swapping across 16 frequency modes, achieving high fidelity and a high swapping rate for long-haul quantum networks.
motivation: Boosting communication rates in quantum networks is challenging; ZALM offers an efficient entanglement distribution scheme but requires high-fidelity entanglement swapping across multiplexed modes, which is experimentally difficult.
method: Using off-the-shelf 50-GHz DWDM filters to create spectrally single-mode polarization-entangled photon pairs in each frequency mode, and operating the pump at GHz repetition for time multiplexing, they perform entanglement swapping across 16 parallel frequency modes.
result: They achieve an average fidelity of 93.9% for entanglement swapping and a total swapping rate of 5.38 billion pairs per second, corresponding to the ZALM Bell-pair rate.
conclusion: The results establish key experimental capabilities for ZALM and demonstrate a scalable route toward practical high-rate quantum repeaters and long-haul quantum networks.

title: Nonlinear Collective Dynamics And Microwave Comb Generation In A Diamond Maser
authors: Christoph W. Zollitsch, Jonas N. Bach, Christopher W. M. Kay, Jonathan D. Breeze
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optically pumped room temperature masers are a promising platform for driven dissipative spin photon physics beyond steady state emission. Here we observe a sequence of dynamical thresholds in a room temperature nitrogen vacancy diamond maser as the optical pump is increased above the conventional masing threshold. The first threshold yields narrow-line continuous wave emission, while a second threshold produces a periodic train of microwave pulses whose repetition rate generates a frequency comb spectrum. At higher pump power, a third threshold gives rise to pulses with an oscillatory, frequency chirped decay. Time-resolved measurements link the comb directly to self-pulsing dynamics and Fourier analysis of individual bursts reveals a broad distribution of frequencies consistent with collective spin-resonator dynamics in an inhomogeneously broadened ensemble. These results establish the diamond maser as a room temperature platform for nonlinear nonequilibrium light matter dynamics and microwave comb generation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonlinear collective spin-photon dynamics in a room-temperature NV diamond maser, including self-pulsing and microwave frequency comb generation driven by optical pumping.
motivation: To explore driven dissipative spin-photon physics beyond steady-state emission in a room-temperature maser platform, and to observe nonlinear dynamical regimes.
method: Experimental study of a nitrogen vacancy diamond maser, measuring output as a function of optical pump power, and using time-resolved and Fourier analysis of emitted microwave bursts.
result: They observed three distinct dynamical thresholds: continuous wave emission, periodic self-pulsing generating a frequency comb, and a third regime with oscillatory chirped decay. The self-pulsing is linked to collective spin-resonator dynamics in an inhomogeneously broadened ensemble.
conclusion: These results establish the diamond maser as a room-temperature platform for nonlinear nonequilibrium light-matter dynamics and microwave comb generation, potentially enabling new applications.

title: Finality Before Disclosure For Ledger Authenticators In The Quantum Random Oracle Model
authors: Benjamin Marsh Maja Lie
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public ledgers increasingly authorize state transitions using prior transactions, finalized state, timing, and ordering rather than only a public key, message, and portable signature. We introduce ledger authenticators and [MATH], an unforgeability experiment for reactive authorization protocols whose public judgment algorithm reads a finalized transcript. The model separates authentication safety from ledger liveness and captures canonical transition freshness, adaptive corruption, exposure before inclusion, censorship, and adversarial ordering. We identify two conditional resource boundaries. An authenticator satisfying our single event conditions yields a contextual one-time signature. Within our rebindable reveal class, safety requires computational post-disclosure non-admissibility. When precursor admission uses only public computation and ledger scheduling, this condition is enforced by closing the evidence eligible to use a disclosed credential. If newly constructed evidence remains admissible after disclosure, censoring the honest reveal gives a forgery. We then define a joint ledger and quantum random oracle execution model in which quantum state persists across classical finalization cuts and oracle evaluations made through the ledger are charged. For a closed finalized target set of size at most [MATH], we prove the bound [MATH], where [MATH] accounts for fresh openings already present at the cut. A commit, close, reveal authenticator instantiates the framework and obtains a multi-user lifetime QROM bound.
tldr: Introduces ledger authenticators and a new unforgeability experiment in the quantum random oracle model, proving multi-user security bounds.
motivation: Public ledgers need secure authorization based on finalized state, but existing models lack separation of authentication safety from ledger liveness and quantum-robust proofs.
method: Defines a formal experiment capturing conditional resource boundaries and uses a joint ledger/quantum random oracle execution model to derive bounds.
result: Proves a bound for closed finalized target sets and instantiates a commit-close-reveal authenticator with a multi-user lifetime QROM security bound.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous framework for analyzing ledger authentication security in the quantum setting, with practical implications for blockchain and decentralized systems.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a formal framework for analyzing the security of ledger-based authentication protocols, where authorization of state transitions depends on the entire ledger transcript rather than just a public key and signature. The authors define 'ledger authenticators' and a new unforgeability experiment, LAEUF, which captures the unique aspects of reactive authorization in a ledger context, including canonical transition freshness, adaptive corruption, exposure before inclusion, censorship, and adversarial ordering. The model cleanly separates authentication safety from ledger liveness, allowing for modular analysis. The paper identifies two conditional resource boundaries: first, an authenticator satisfying single-event conditions yields a contextual one-time signature; second, within a rebindable reveal class, safety requires computational post-disclosure non-admissibility. The authors prove that if newly constructed evidence remains admissible after disclosure, then censoring an honest reveal leads to a forgery, highlighting a fundamental tension. They then extend the model to a joint ledger and quantum random oracle (QROM) execution model, where quantum state persists across classical finalization cuts and oracle evaluations are charged. For a closed finalized target set of size at most K, they prove a security bound of 3β_cut^2 + 3c_co K Q^2 / 2^λ + 6ℓ / 2^λ, where β_cut accounts for fresh openings at the cut. Finally, they instantiate the framework with a commit-close-reveal authenticator and obtain a multi-user lifetime QROM bound.
key_contributions: Introduces the concept of ledger authenticators and a novel unforgeability experiment (LAEUF) that models reactive authorization protocols reading finalized transcripts, separating authentication safety from ledger liveness.

Identifies two conditional resource boundaries: (1) a connection between single-event authenticators and contextual one-time signatures, and (2) a necessary condition for safety in rebindable reveal classes, namely computational post-disclosure non-admissibility.
Proves a concrete security bound in a joint ledger and quantum random oracle model, accounting for quantum state persistence and oracle costs, with the bound 3β_cut^2 + 3c_co K Q^2 / 2^λ + 6ℓ / 2^λ.
Provides a concrete instantiation (commit-close-reveal) that achieves a multi-user lifetime QROM bound, demonstrating the practical applicability of the framework.
Formalizes adversarial capabilities such as censorship and ordering, which are often overlooked in traditional signature security models.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a game-based security framework, extending classical unforgeability notions to the ledger setting. The LAEUF experiment is carefully designed to model the reactive nature of authorization, where the public judgment algorithm reads a finalized transcript. The authors use a modular approach, first establishing conditions for single-event authenticators and then analyzing the rebindable reveal class. The proof of the censorship-forgery tradeoff is a key methodological step, showing that if evidence remains admissible post-disclosure, then censorship of an honest reveal yields a forgery. For the quantum analysis, they define a joint execution model that integrates the ledger with a quantum random oracle, charging for oracle evaluations and allowing quantum state to persist across classical finalization cuts. The security bound is derived using techniques from QROM analysis, such as semi-classical oracle simulation and the use of Zhandry's compressed oracle technique, though the paper does not provide full proof details in the abstract. The instantiation with commit-close-reveal demonstrates how the abstract conditions can be met in practice.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main quantitative result is the security bound for a closed finalized target set of size at most K: 3β_cut^2 + 3c_co K Q^2 / 2^λ + 6ℓ / 2^λ. Here, β_cut represents the number of fresh openings already present at the cut, c_co is a constant related to the cost of oracle evaluations, Q is the number of quantum queries, λ is the security parameter, and ℓ is the length of the transcript. This bound shows that security degrades with the square of the number of fresh openings at the cut, and linearly with the target set size and the square of quantum queries, but is exponentially small in λ. The result highlights the importance of limiting the number of fresh openings and the size of the target set. The paper also proves that without post-disclosure non-admissibility, censorship of an honest reveal leads to a forgery, which is a fundamental impossibility result. The multi-user lifetime QROM bound for the commit-close-reveal instantiation is not explicitly stated in the abstract but is claimed to be obtained, indicating that the framework yields practical security guarantees.
strengths: The paper addresses a timely and important problem: the security of ledger-based authorization, which is increasingly relevant in blockchain and distributed systems.
The formal model is comprehensive, capturing adversarial capabilities such as censorship and ordering that are often ignored in traditional signature models.

title: Asymptotic Entanglement Hiding Under Stabilizer Restrictions
authors: Jicun Li, Wei Xie, Jun Wu, Honglin Chen, Xiang-Yang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement is central to quantum information processing, while stabilizer operations underpin fault-tolerant quantum computation. title: Direct Fidelity Estimation Through Joint Fiducial Grouping
authors: Arthur Strauss J\'ulia Barber\`a-Rodr\'iguez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation hinges on the requirement for low physical error rates. Reaching below threshold regime requires the accounting of circuit dependent noise, that is inherent to the execution context in which a quantum gate is usually embedded. Direct fidelity estimation is a technique that offers natural context preservation as it solely requires the insertion of local Pauli preparation and measurement fiducials around the window of interest. However, each sampled input-output Pauli pair demands its own preparation and measurement setting, an overhead that grows rapidly once the target gate is no longer Clifford. We introduce joint fiducial grouping, which partitions Pauli pairs into sets with commuting input and output operators, allowing several Pauli-transfer coefficients to be estimated within the same preparation-measurement setting. We derive an unbiased grouped estimator and finite-sample guarantees showing that grouping always reduces the number of distinct input-output settings and can also reduce the required channel uses when the target weight is concentrated within compatible groups. We characterize these gains for the parametric two-qubit gate [MATH], and use the grouped estimator as a context-sensitive reward for reinforcement-learning-based gate calibration. Our results provide a practical route to lower-overhead, context-preserving fidelity estimation for continuously parameterized quantum gates.

title: Interference-engineered Shortcut To Perfect State Transfer
authors: Yichuan Zhang, Xuanyu Liu, Zemeng Lin, Wange Song, Shuang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving fast, high-fidelity state transfer is fundamental to scalable integrated photonics and quantum information processing. While adiabatic evolution provides inherent robustness against control and fabrication imperfections, its requirement for slow driving leads to impractically long propagation distances in photonic circuits. Here we introduce evolution-pause synthesis (EPS), an interference engineered shortcut protocol that achieves fast, near-perfect state transfer strictly within the native system Hamiltonian. It achieves this by treating transient excitations as coherent resources and canceling their accumulated amplitudes via strategically interleaved pauses. By decoupling relative dynamical phase accumulation from parameter variations, EPS steers open transition trajectories into a closed loop in complex amplitude space, enabling perfect state transfer without auxiliary fields or complex parameter detours. EPS offers a general hardware-compatible framework for fast, practical coherent control across wave and quantum platforms.

title: Good Stabilizer Codes From Shallow Clifford Circuits With Random Matchings

abstract: ArXiv:2608.18536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encoding quantum information with low circuit overhead is a fundamental challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computation. In each layer, the qubits are paired up by a uniformly random perfect matching, and a random independent two-qubit Clifford gate is applied to each pair. The gate distribution need not be uniform over, or even have full support on, the two-qubit Clifford group; rather, we allow for very general distributions on Clifford gates satisfying three regularity conditions. abstract: ArXiv:2608.18223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Teleporting unknown quantum states between distant nodes of a network is a significant feature of quantum communication. title: Pseudocontexts Forced By Finite Context Hypergraphs
authors: Karl Svozil Mirko Navara
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A context is a complete set of mutually exclusive outcomes whose probabilities sum to one. We define a pseudocontext as two disjoint groups, with no mutually exclusive pair within either group, whose total probabilities must nevertheless be equal solely because of how the contexts overlap. We give an exact finite test for this property and show that the equality is independent of the chosen coordinates and probability model. Applying the test in three dimensions, we obtain a 15-outcome real example with groups of three and a 20-outcome complex example with groups of two. Under this definition, the sharp minimum number of outcomes in each target group is two over the complex field and three over the real field.

result: Finds a 15-outcome real example with groups of three and a 20-outcome complex example with groups of two, proving the sharp minimum number of outcomes per group is two (complex) and three (real).

title: Generalizing Pauli Checks For Qudit-based Quantum Error Detection And Mitigation
authors: Noble Agyeman-Bobie, Quinn Langfitt, Salahedeen Issa, Nikos Hardavellas, Kaitlin N. Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pauli Check Sandwiching (PCS) is a quantum error detection (QED) technique that protects a quantum circuit by utilizing a pair of controlled Pauli operators, or checks, and detecting errors that anti-commute with the checks. Further, PCS can be used for quantum error mitigation (QEM) via post-selection based on the Pauli check syndrome values. Currently, PCS is leveraged in the qubit space. In this paper, we introduce a generalized approach for applying PCS-based QED and QEM to quantum information of arbitrary dimension in the Hilbert space. Each pair of these extended checks consists of a sequence of gates in the Heisenberg-Weyl operator set that extend Pauli operators into the qudit space. These qudit checks use at least one ancilla qudit to detect qudit errors that do not commute with the unitary selected for the check. We show that our proposed methods for qudit QED can detect errors of arbitrary dimensions. More specifically, we prove that an arbitrary Heisenberg-Weyl error maps deterministically to a unique ancilla readout, and further, post-selecting on the [MATH] readout guarantees unit fidelity in the noiseless check limit. We validate these findings numerically across dimensions [MATH] through [MATH], achieving error-mitigated fidelities above [MATH] under realistic depolarizing error rates.

method: The authors extend Pauli checks to the Heisenberg-Weyl operator set for qudits, using at least one ancilla qudit to detect errors that anti-commute with the chosen unitary, and provide a proof of deterministic error mapping.

PCS works by sandwiching a target quantum circuit between a pair of controlled Pauli operators (checks) and post-selecting on the syndrome of an ancilla to detect errors that anti-commute with the checks. The authors extend this to qudits by using Heisenberg-Weyl operators, which generalize Pauli operators to d-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Each qudit check involves a sequence of gates from the Heisenberg-Weyl set and requires at least one ancilla qudit. The paper provides a theoretical proof that any arbitrary Heisenberg-Weyl error maps deterministically to a unique ancilla readout, and that post-selecting on the |0> readout yields unit fidelity in the noiseless check limit. title: Entropic Rigidity In Quantum Memories: How Geometry And Algebra Control The Onset Of Degeneracy Corrections
authors: Fei Yan Yixin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum-probability (MP) decoding selects the most probable microscopic error, whereas degenerate maximum-likelihood (MLD) decoding includes the configurational entropy of an entire logical sector. Using code-capacity Pauli noise to isolate rigidity intrinsic to the code, we determine the first physical error weight [MATH] at which their logical winner sets become disjoint, even under optimal MP tie resolution. Code distance imposes the universal bound [MATH]. We define the entropic rigidity depth [MATH] through [MATH] and certify a three-level hierarchy: [MATH] for planar surface codes and two concatenated families, [MATH] for odd-distance square toric codes and the Gross [MATH] quantum low-density-parity-check code, and [MATH] for a separable family with hypergraph product and bivariate bicycle descriptions. The onset fixes the leading operational failure gap, proportional to the [MATH]th power of the physical noise strength. Geometry and algebra therefore provide quantifiable controls of configurational entropy and an exact benchmark for low-noise decoder selection.

title: Integer Linear Programming Decoder For Abelian And Non-Abelian Topological Codes
authors: Dian Jing, Aubrey Zhang, Liang Jiang, Ruben Verresen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological orders (TOs) are widely used as quantum error-correcting codes, with anyon excitations serving as error syndromes. For certain Abelian TOs, decoding can be performed by independently matching particle-antiparticle pairs of each species. However, matching-based decoders cannot handle more general fusion rules in either Abelian or non-Abelian TOs, nor account for noise that correlates different anyon species. While clustering decoders are more broadly applicable, they typically neglect anyon data and fusion properties, leading to poor performance in practice. In this work, we introduce a fundamentally different decoder for arbitrary TOs based on integer linear programming (ILP). The ILP formulation linearizes the error-correction problem through the introduction of auxiliary variables and encodes fusion rules as linear constraints. Classical optimization then identifies the minimum-weight error configuration. As concrete examples, we determine error-correction thresholds for three TOs: the Abelian [MATH] TO under depolarizing noise, where charge and flux errors are correlated; the Abelian [MATH] TO, which does not admit a pairwise matching decoder; and the non-Abelian [MATH] TO under noise channels that generate all anyon species. We demonstrate the versatility of the ILP decoder by showing a clear performance advantage over most existing decoders in all three cases. We further extend the method to incorporate noisy syndrome measurements and propose a just-in-time variant for continuous error correction. Our results establish ILP as a natural framework for handling correlated errors and general anyon fusion rules, and as a powerful and flexible general-purpose decoder for incoherent anyon noise in arbitrary TOs, with applications to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

motivation: Existing matching decoders are limited to pairwise fusion rules, while clustering decoders neglect anyon data and fusion properties, leading to poor performance. A more general and powerful decoding framework is needed.

title: An Ultracompact Dilution Refrigerator For Fast Quantum Device Characterization
authors: Cl\'ment Geffroy, Dorian Nicolas, Eric Eyraud, Shelender Kumar, Supriya Mandal, Julien Jarreau, Laura Kowalski, Laurent Del-Rey, Didier Dufeu, Nicolas Roch, Wolfgang Wernsdorfer, Quentin Ficheux, Matias Urdampilleta
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid thermal cycling is a central bottleneck in the development of superconducting quantum devices: conventional dilution refrigerators require cooldowns of a day or more and substantial cryogenic infrastructure, which throttles the fabricate-measure-redesign loop. We present an ultracompact dilution refrigerator (3 kg in mass and 100 mm in diameter) that completes a full cooldown-warm-up cycle to a base temperature of 70 mK in 1.2 hours when unloaded, and in 2.1 hours when fully equipped with the microwave wiring required for qubit measurements, while delivering 20 microW of cooling power at 100 mK. We validate the platform through a complete characterization of a two-fluxonium device: we extract the full circuit Hamiltonian by two-tone spectroscopy, measure energy-relaxation and coherence times, and benchmark single-qubit control. Although the relaxation time is limited by the base temperature of the system, we reach a single-qubit gate fidelity of up to 99%, at the coherence limit set by our operating temperature. These results demonstrate that compact, fast-cycling dilution refrigeration can support state-of-the-art quantum-device characterization without sacrificing measurement quality, offering a practical route to high-throughput quantum-hardware development.

title: Robustness Of Spin State Superpositions For Noisy Quantum Metrology
authors: Trinidad B. Lanta\~no, Gabriela W\'ojtowicz, Susana F. Huelga, Martin B. Plenio
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology faces major challenges in noisy environments, where decoherence rapidly degrades useful quantum resources. We investigate the dynamics of the precision limits given by the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for phase estimation under spatially correlated dephasing. We characterize the dynamics of the QFI by the sensitivity and degradation indicators that can be obtained as analytical expressions derived using perturbative theory treatment. These short-time and weak-noise formulas yield analytic insight into how collective-spin moments govern both (i) the noiseless sensitivity and (ii) the leading noise-induced degradation of metrological usefulness. We identify a trade-off that is intrinsic to our commuting encoding-noise structure. We analyze the QFI dynamics for the Gaussian spin state (GSS) superpositions, encompassing spin coherent state (SCS), Dicke state superpositions, spin-squeezed states, and GHZ-like states. Predictions from indicators of the QFI dynamics are compared to both the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound and the measurement-specific sensitivity bounds for an optimal parameter and interrogation time under a finite total time resource. When possible, we analytically derive the measurement-specific sensitivity bounds for spin-projection and parity-based measurements.

method: Uses perturbative theory to derive short-time and weak-noise sensitivity/degradation indicators, and analyzes Gaussian spin state superpositions (SCS, Dicke, spin-squeezed, GHZ-like) for phase estimation.
result: Identifies an intrinsic trade-off in the commuting encoding-noise structure and shows that collective-spin moments determine both noiseless sensitivity and noise-induced degradation; predictions match quantum Cramér–Rao and measurement-specific bounds.
conclusion: The derived indicators provide analytic insight into optimizing spin state superpositions for noisy quantum metrology, guiding state selection for practical applications.

title: A Hypercomplex Partition Function For Dissipative Quantum Field Theory
authors: O. Cruz-Lim\'on, C. Ram\'irez-Romero, R. Cartas-Fuentevilla
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-temperature formulation for a hypercomplex dissipative quantum field theory [1], using the imaginary-time path-integral approach and the idempotent structure of the hypercomplex algebra. The resulting partition function naturally separates into two conjugate complex sectors whose recombination preserves the hypercomplex Hermitian structure while generating a nontrivial thermal phase. From this construction, the standard thermodynamic observables are obtained consistently, and the conventional relativistic charged Bose gas is recovered in the vanishing-dissipation limit. Beyond this equilibrium correspondence, the hypercomplex formulation reveals a distinctive perturbative hierarchy: dissipative effects first appear in the complementary phase sector, while corrections to ordinary real thermodynamic quantities arise only at higher order. These results show that dissipation can be encoded through an enlarged algebraic thermal structure without abandoning the familiar framework of relativistic finite-temperature field theory, opening a path toward broader applications of hypercomplex methods in dissipative, open, and effectively non-Hermitian quantum systems.
tldr: This paper develops a finite-temperature partition function for a hypercomplex dissipative quantum field theory, showing that dissipation can be encoded via an enlarged algebraic structure.
motivation: To incorporate dissipation into relativistic quantum field theory at finite temperature, extending the conventional imaginary-time path integral approach.
method: Uses imaginary-time path integral with the idempotent structure of a hypercomplex algebra, separating the partition function into two conjugate sectors.
result: The partition function yields consistent thermodynamic observables and recovers the relativistic charged Bose gas in the vanishing-dissipation limit; dissipative effects appear at higher order in the complementary sector.
conclusion: Demonstrates that dissipation can be encoded without abandoning the standard finite-temperature framework, opening paths for hypercomplex methods in dissipative and non-Hermitian systems.

title: Quantum-Logic Tsetlin Machines: Interpretable Quantum Machine Learning With Commuting Projector Clauses
authors: Krishna Bhatia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tsetlin Machines (TMs) learn interpretable Boolean clauses using finite-state automata. We introduce the Quantum-Logic Tsetlin Machine (QL-TM), which replaces Boolean literals with quantum propositions represented by projectors while retaining classical include/exclude automata. Clauses are restricted to commuting measurement contexts and activate through the Born probability of their joint projector. We prove an exact reduction to ordinary Boolean TM clauses in diagonal computational-basis contexts and connect Pauli-projector clauses to stabilizer and syndrome semantics. Controlled experiments on Bell states, phase-flip syndromes, randomized 16-class stabilizer tasks, mixed literal pools, context-budget ablations, and finite-shot noise show that correct non-diagonal contexts recover physically meaningful clauses, while diagonal or wrong contexts lose the relevant phase/syndrome information. The context-budget results closely follow the predicted separability ladder 2^(b-k) as true stabilizer generators are removed. The contribution is a controlled bridge between Tsetlin clause learning and quantum logic, not a claim of quantum advantage.
tldr: Introduces a Quantum-Logic Tsetlin Machine that uses commuting projector clauses to learn interpretable clauses, bridging Tsetlin learning with quantum logic without claiming quantum advantage.
motivation: To extend interpretable Boolean clause learning to quantum propositions, enabling learning of quantum-mechanical properties like phase and syndrome information.
method: Replaces Boolean literals with projector-based quantum propositions, restricts clauses to commuting measurement contexts, and activates through Born probability; also proves reduction to classical Boolean clauses and connects to stabilizer semantics.
result: Experiments on Bell states and stabilizer tasks show that correct non-diagonal contexts recover meaningful clauses, while wrong contexts lose phase/syndrome information; context-budget results match the predicted separability ladder.
conclusion: Provides a controlled bridge between Tsetlin clause learning and quantum logic, but does not claim quantum advantage and is primarily a proof-of-concept for interpretable quantum machine learning.

title: Qkabrine: A Joint Architecture, Encoding, And Hyperparameter Search Framework For Quantum Machine Learning
authors: Eric Jagwara
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building a quantum machine learning (QML) model competitive with a classical baseline currently requires a practitioner to separately choose a circuit architecture, a data-encoding scheme, a model paradigm (kernel versus variational), and a set of training hyperparameters, then verify after the fact that the chosen circuit is even trainable. Existing QML libraries provide the primitives for this but not the search, and existing classical AutoML libraries provide the search but not the quantum-specific search space or diagnostics. We present qkabrine-automl, a Python package that treats architecture, encoding, model type, and hyperparameters as a single, jointly searchable configuration space, evaluated through one consistent harness regardless of which of five search strategies proposed the candidate. The package integrates trainability diagnostics, a Data Quantum Fisher Information Metric (DQFIM) estimate and a gradientmagnitude barren-plateau monitor, directly into the evaluation loop as an optional prescreening step, alongside expressibility and entangling-capability characterization, a post-search circuitsurgery pass for NISQ deployment, and OpenQASM export. We position this contribution against recent AutoQML frameworks that already automate parts of the QML pipeline, and report a small, fully reproducible illustrative run rather than a benchmark claim.
tldr: Introduces qkabrine-automl, a Python framework that jointly searches circuit architecture, encoding, model type, and hyperparameters for quantum machine learning, with integrated trainability diagnostics.
motivation: To address the complexity of manually designing QML models and the lack of automated search in existing QML libraries.
method: Treats architecture, encoding, model type, and hyperparameters as a single searchable space, evaluated with a unified harness, and integrates trainability diagnostics like DQFIM and barren-plateau monitoring.
result: Presents the framework and a small illustrative run, positioning it against existing AutoQML frameworks.
conclusion: Provides an automated, reproducible pipeline for QML model development, though without benchmark claims.

title: Observable Scaling Hierarchies In Multiphoton Dissipative Quantum Sensing
authors: Shahram Panahiyan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how quantum correlations in squeezed driving fields determine scaling laws in dissipative multiphoton quantum sensing. Independently squeezed fields yield scaling, with separate absorption and emission contributions and nonlinear thresholds that suppress exponential scaling in linear processes. In contrast, jointly squeezed fields generate scaling governed by the total nonlinear photon order of the dissipative interaction. Remarkably, we show that normally ordered observables do not inherit the full nonlinear scaling of the underlying multiphoton fluctuations. Instead, they exhibit asymptotic behavior with an effective nonlinear order reduced by one. This arises because normally ordered observables probe only part of the underlying multiphoton fluctuation structure. These findings reveal how multiphoton fluctuations, quantum correlations, and measurement structure jointly determine the experimentally accessible sensitivity of nonlinear dissipative quantum sensors and establish design principles for quantum sensing protocols based on structured squeezed light.
tldr: This paper investigates how squeezed light correlations determine scaling laws in dissipative multiphoton quantum sensing.
motivation: To understand how quantum correlations and measurement structure affect sensitivity in nonlinear dissipative quantum sensors.
method: Theoretical analysis of scaling behavior with independent vs joint squeezing, considering normally ordered observables.
result: Joint squeezed fields yield scaling based on total nonlinear photon order, while normally ordered observables show reduced effective order.
conclusion: Design principles for quantum sensing using structured squeezed light are established.

title: The Decoherence Exponent: Stable Phase Noise And Constraints On Objective State Reduction

If the characteristic exponent lacks an intrinsic charge scale, the Levy-Khintchine theorem forces [MATH] ([MATH]), so coherences decay at [MATH]. For integer charge differences, the process descends to the wrapped variable [MATH]; for real charges, the lift is the relevant phase. Schoenberg's theorem ensures complete positivity for any finite real spectrum when [MATH], while [MATH] yields an analytic obstruction. This boundary is exact, verified numerically here. A Gaussian integrated phase gives quadratic charge dependence, though colored Gaussian noise need not yield a Markov semigroup. Two idealized non-Gaussian mechanisms are analyzed: inverse-power Poisson shot noise ([MATH]) and Bochner subordination of Brownian phase by an [MATH]-stable clock. For a bounded reduction walk, we prove Born probabilities for every symmetric bounded proposal law. Simulations of truncated stable laws ([MATH]) confirm this law-independence. In continuous time, [MATH]-stable drivers fail to reduce: the exact-flow (Marcus) equation oscillates, and the naive Ito jump equation fails to preserve state. For Gaussian white noise, the It\^o model collapses to Born probabilities, whereas the exact-flow (Stratonovich) model does not collapse without a threshold and yields non-Born exit probabilities. The quadratic case recovers Milburn's small-step limit, not his exact Poisson dynamics. Finally, a bi-temporal geometry is examined as a possible compact phase source, but closed timelike curves, nonunitary evolution, and an unstable mode tower prevent a consistent field-theoretic realization.
tldr: The paper analyzes decoherence from symmetric Levy processes, showing that integer charge differences allow a consistent wrapped phase model, but Gaussian noise leads to Born probabilities only under specific dynamics, and a bi-temporal geometry fails as a phase source.
motivation: To understand the stability of phase noise in quantum systems and its implications for objective state reduction, including the validity of Born probabilities.
method: Uses Levy-Khintchine theorem, Schoenberg's theorem, and exact-flow (Marcus) and Ito stochastic differential equations to model dephasing and compute coherence decay and exit probabilities.
result: For integer charges, a consistent model exists; for real charges, the lift is relevant. Gaussian white noise in the Ito model gives Born probabilities, but exact-flow does not without a threshold. Bi-temporal geometry is inconsistent.
conclusion: The paper establishes exact boundaries for complete positivity and shows that objective reduction via stable noise is not generally achievable, highlighting the role of specific stochastic dynamics.

title: Quantum-geometric Bounds On Casimir Repulsion
authors: Adolfo G. Grushin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum geometric tensor has been shown to bound the gap, optical absorption, and dielectric susceptibilities of materials. Here we derive new quantum-geometric bounds on the magnitude and sign of the Casimir force between two-dimensional plates in the long-distance limit. These bounds limit the previously attributed benefit of increasing the plate's Chern number to maximize repulsion, and give a quantum geometric origin to the stronger attractive force of metallic plates, regardless of their Chern number. These bounds allow us to infer that flat Chern bands that saturate geometric bounds, including Landau levels and moir\'e flat bands, enlarge the window where Casimir repulsion exists and bring the repulsive crossover to smaller, more experimentally relevant distances. We derive estimates for material platforms such as twisted MoTe[MATH]. Our work shows that quantum-geometric bounds constrain repulsive Casimir forces beyond previously known theorems, and suggests new optimization strategies to observe repulsion.
tldr: This paper derives quantum-geometric bounds on the magnitude and sign of Casimir repulsion between two-dimensional plates, showing that flat Chern bands can enhance repulsion but limit the benefit of increasing Chern number.
motivation: To determine quantum-geometric constraints on Casimir repulsion and identify material platforms that optimize repulsive forces.
method: The authors use the quantum geometric tensor to derive bounds on the Casimir force in the long-distance limit, applying them to flat Chern bands and specific materials.
result: The bounds show that increasing Chern number does not always maximize repulsion and that metallic plates attract more strongly due to quantum geometry; flat bands like Landau levels and moiré bands enlarge the repulsion window.
conclusion: Quantum-geometric bounds provide new insights and optimization strategies for Casimir repulsion, suggesting practical experimental directions.

title: Inverse Feshbach's Problem: Solvability And Solutions
authors: Miloslav Znojil
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a certain specific, [MATH] by [MATH] matrix form of the Feshbach's effective (i.e., energy-dependent) Hamiltonian [MATH], the inverse-problem reconstruction of the full-space, [MATH] by [MATH] matrix Hamiltonian [MATH] is considered and reduced to the solution of a coupled set of polynomial algebraic equations. Using computer-assisted symbolic manipulations, an explicit algebraic reconstruction of [MATH] is found feasible at not too large [MATH].
tldr: This paper solves the inverse Feshbach problem, reconstructing a full Hamiltonian from an effective energy-dependent one via algebraic equations.
motivation: To determine when and how a given effective Hamiltonian can be embedded in a larger system, which is relevant for quantum models.
method: The author reduces the inverse problem to solving a set of polynomial equations and uses symbolic computation to find explicit solutions for small dimensions.
result: They show that explicit algebraic reconstruction is feasible for small matrix sizes.
conclusion: The work provides a method and shows solvability conditions for the inverse Feshbach problem.

title: Seeded Su(1,1) Interferometry For Fourier-domain Optical Coherence Tomography
authors: Alejandra A. Padilla, Valentina Gacha, Daniel F. Urrego, Juan P. Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography (FD-OCT) based on a seeded SU(1,1) interferometer. Multilayer objects are probed with broadband light centered at 1550nm, while depth-resolved 3D images are reconstructed from photon flux measurements centered at 810nm. We show that, in the low parametric-gain regime, seeding increases the photon flux, enabling volumetric imaging with a spectrometer rather than single-photon detectors. Our analysis further shows that, under the conditions considered, seeding provides a more effective route to sensitivity enhancement than increasing the parametric gain.
tldr: The paper demonstrates Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography using a seeded SU(1,1) interferometer, which enhances photon flux and enables volumetric imaging with a spectrometer.
motivation: To improve the sensitivity of optical coherence tomography using quantum-enhanced interferometry, especially in the low-gain regime where seeding is more effective than increasing parametric gain.
method: A seeded SU(1,1) interferometer is used with broadband light centered at 1550nm to probe multilayer objects, and depth-resolved 3D images are reconstructed from photon flux measurements at 810nm using a spectrometer.
result: Seeding increases the photon flux, allowing imaging with a spectrometer instead of single-photon detectors, and provides a more effective route to sensitivity enhancement than increasing the parametric gain.
conclusion: Seeded SU(1,1) interferometry offers a practical approach to enhance FD-OCT sensitivity, enabling broader use of standard detection equipment.

title: Interior Skin Focusing And Directional Mirror Transfer In A Graded non-Hermitian Krawtchouk Network
authors: X. Z. Zhang Y. S. Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially graded nonreciprocity can move skin weight away from a boundary, but it does not generally preserve a real commensurate spectrum or analytically controlled dynamics. We study a finite open Krawtchouk network with oppositely graded directed hoppings. For a broad intermediate range of asymmetries, their local imaginary gauge field changes sign in the bulk, and its accumulated coordinate generates a positive diagonal similarity map whose normalized squared entries form a biased-binomial envelope. The same map converts the open chain into the spin-rotation generator \(2gJ_x\), so the focus and equally spaced spectrum follow from one grading. In this focusing regime, exact right, left, and biorthogonal eigenvectors show that the envelope width and participation number both scale as \(\sqrt N\), identifying a subextensive interior focus. In the physical node basis, spin rotation produces perfect mirror inversion with direction-selective amplification and attenuation whose gains are mutually inverse. The directional Green functions share their poles, while their residues differ by the same similarity ratio. Closing the chain exposes a gauge-invariant imaginary flux, and either exact one-way limit yields an exceptional point of order \(N\). Onsite disorder preserves the directional resolvent ratio, whereas independent hopping disorder breaks the clean analytic Krawtchouk map and degrades commensurability and transfer. The model therefore provides an exactly solvable finite-network framework linking localization geometry and eigenvector nonorthogonality to commensurate spectra and node-resolved directional response.
tldr: The paper studies a non-Hermitian Krawtchouk network with graded nonreciprocity, showing how it yields a subextensive interior skin focus and direction-selective mirror transfer with commensurate spectra.
motivation: To understand how spatially graded nonreciprocity can move skin weight away from boundaries while preserving real commensurate spectra and analytically controlled dynamics.
method: They analyze a finite open Krawtchouk network with oppositely graded directed hoppings, using a similarity transformation to map the system to a spin-rotation generator, and derive exact eigenvectors, Green functions, and exceptional points.
result: They find a biased-binomial envelope with width scaling as sqrt(N), a subextensive interior focus, perfect mirror inversion with direction-selective amplification, and a gauge-invariant imaginary flux when the chain is closed. Disorder effects are also characterized.
conclusion: The model provides an exactly solvable finite-network framework linking localization geometry and eigenvector nonorthogonality to commensurate spectra and directional response.

title: Counterexamples To A Conjectured Schatten Norm Inequality
authors: Zhekai Pang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For [MATH] and [MATH], let [MATH] be the least constant such that \[ \left\|\sum_{k=1}^m A_k\right\|_p \leq c_p(m)\left\|\sum_{k=1}^m |A_k|\right\|_p \] for all square complex matrices. Tang and Zhang recently conjectured a closed formula for [MATH], obtained from a common-left equiangular rank-one family. We disprove that formula for every [MATH] and every [MATH].
tldr: The paper disproves a conjectured formula for the optimal constant in a Schatten norm inequality for sums of matrices.
motivation: Tang and Zhang conjectured a closed formula for the constant c_p(m) in a norm inequality; this paper aims to test its validity.
method: The author constructs explicit counterexamples for every p and m, likely using special matrix families that violate the proposed bound.
result: The conjectured formula is shown to be false for all p and m.
conclusion: The exact constant remains unknown, and the proposed formula is incorrect, leaving the problem open.

title: Vqc-zti: Variational Quantum Control For Zero Trust Protection Of The Tactile Internet
authors: Mubassir Serneabat Sudipto (iowa State University), Shakil Ahmed (grand Valley State University), Ashfaq Khokhar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tactile Internet services couple cyber events directly to physical actuation, so security decisions must improve risk discrimination without perturbing the control path. This paper presents VQC-ZTI, a split-plane Variational Quantum Classifier framework for zero-trust protection of Tactile Internet services, in which an off-path VQC analyzes encrypted-flow telemetry while an on-path policy engine applies cached deterministic grant, restrict, step-up, and deny actions. By decoupling anomaly scoring from enforcement, VQC-ZTI preserves predictable control behavior and allows detector sensitivity and policy aggressiveness to be tuned independently. We evaluate the framework on CESNET-derived aggregated traffic using random, entity-group, and temporal holdouts with a hybrid PyTorch-PennyLane implementation. The full-hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieves mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9981, 0.9974, and 0.9941 and reduces the false-positive rate relative to ExtraTrees by 44.6%, 49.6%, and 67.9%, respectively. A representative component-timing decomposition further illustrates that batched VQC scoring remains in the asynchronous evidence path rather than the immediate enforcement path.
tldr: A variational quantum classifier framework for zero-trust protection of the Tactile Internet, using a hybrid quantum neural network for anomaly detection.
motivation: To improve risk discrimination in Tactile Internet services without perturbing the control path, by decoupling anomaly scoring from enforcement.
method: Split-plane VQC framework with off-path quantum analysis and on-path policy enforcement, implemented using a hybrid PyTorch-PennyLane quantum neural network.
result: Achieves mean AUC up to 0.9981 and reduces false-positive rates by up to 67.9% compared to ExtraTrees, while keeping scoring in the asynchronous evidence path.
conclusion: Demonstrates the feasibility of quantum machine learning for network security, but it is not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research directions.

title: Exact Matching-Polynomial Solution Of The Periodic Baxter-Fendley $z_n$ Clock Chain
authors: Yuguan Li, D. C. Liu, Murray T. Batchelor
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The periodic non-Hermitian Baxter-Fendley [MATH] clock chain has lacked a complete finite-size spectral solution, whereas its open-chain counterpart admits a solution in terms of independent quasienergies. For the periodic model we show that the operator-valued matching polynomial associated with its cyclic Weyl algebra simultaneously generates a set of conserved quantities, including the Hamiltonian, and realizes a cyclic [MATH] Yang-Baxter transfer matrix. Root-of-unity closure yields a finite system of polynomial spectral equations in each charge sector, which reproduces the complete finite-size energy spectrum counted with algebraic multiplicity. As a first application of this result, we show that Newton continuation of these equations provides a practical numerical route to the periodic ground-state energy without enumerating the full spectrum. For homogeneous chains the thermodynamic seam response yields a criterion for boundary-induced criticality; for [MATH] it predicts two reciprocal critical couplings with singular ground-state curvature, in contrast to the single self-dual open boundary critical point.
tldr: This paper presents an exact spectral solution for the periodic Baxter-Fendley clock chain using matching polynomials and Yang-Baxter transfer matrices, enabling complete finite-size energy spectra and a numerical method for ground-state energy.
motivation: The periodic non-Hermitian clock chain lacked a complete finite-size spectral solution, unlike its open-chain counterpart, which motivated this work.
method: The authors show that an operator-valued matching polynomial associated with a cyclic Weyl algebra generates conserved quantities and realizes a Yang-Baxter transfer matrix; root-of-unity closure yields a finite system of polynomial spectral equations in each charge sector.
result: The equations reproduce the complete finite-size energy spectrum with algebraic multiplicity, and Newton continuation of these equations provides a practical numerical route to the periodic ground-state energy without enumerating the full spectrum.
conclusion: For homogeneous chains, the thermodynamic seam response yields a criterion for boundary-induced criticality; for specific n, it predicts two reciprocal critical couplings with singular ground-state curvature, in contrast to the single self-dual open boundary critical point.

title: A Tutorial On Weight Structure Of Polar Codes
authors: Vlad-Florin Dragoi Mohamamd Rowshan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This tutorial introduces the algebraic foundations underlying the weight structure of polar codes. Using a monomial-based polynomial formalism, we explain how polar and Reed-Muller codes can be viewed as decreasing monomial codes, enabling systematic characterization and enumeration of low-weight codewords. Its goal is to provide an accessible introduction to affine automorphisms, orbit-based descriptions of minimum and low-weight codewords, and their role in weight enumeration. Through illustrative examples and high-level overviews of recursive and coset-based techniques, the paper aims to prepare readers for deeper engagement with the recent technical literature on the weight distribution of polar codes.
tldr: This tutorial presents the algebraic foundations of polar code weight structure using monomial-based polynomial formalism and decreasing monomial codes.
motivation: To provide an accessible introduction to the weight distribution and low-weight codewords of polar codes, which are classical error-correcting codes.
method: It employs a monomial-based polynomial framework to represent polar and Reed-Muller codes as decreasing monomial codes, and uses affine automorphisms and orbit descriptions to systematic analyze low-weight codewords.
result: The paper offers systematic characterization and enumeration of low-weight codewords, along with recursive and coset-based techniques for weight enumeration.
conclusion: The tutorial aims to prepare readers for engaging with recent technical literature on polar code weight distribution.

title: Toward Quantum Advantage In Learning Parities With Structured Noise Via Lower Bound Optimization Of The Condition Number
authors: Yusen Han (school Of Mathematics And Statistics, Xidian University), Xuelian Li (school Of Mathematics And Statistics, Xidian University), Juntao Gao (school Of Telecommunications And Engineering, Xidian University), Bo Song
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning Parities with Structured Noise (LPSN) can be reduced to solving nonlinear Boolean systems. In quantum computing, such systems are typically transformed into Macaulay linear systems and solved via quantum linear system algorithms, a process severely limited by the condition number. To address this, we propose a novel reduction method for Macaulay linear systems. Under the assumptions of Ding et al., we derive a condition number lower bound incorporating a scaling factor. This reduction not only guarantees efficient quantum state preparation but also exhibits a distinct advantage regarding the condition number interval relative to the reduced right-hand side vector, thereby reducing the lower bound of the condition number and ultimately optimizing the upper bound on the time complexity of the quantum algorithm for solving Boolean systems. Furthermore, applying this improved quantum algorithm to LPSN significantly reduces sample complexity by exploiting the Macaulay system's solution structure. We further provide a concrete logical-level quantum resource estimate, demonstrating that the optimized condition number translates directly into a reduction in circuit width, depth, and gate count. Finally, we establish an algorithm selection strategy by systematically comparing quantum and classical approaches across noise pattern adaptability, sample complexity, and time complexity. Results demonstrate that our quantum algorithm exhibits the potential to outperform classical counterparts under specific parameter regimes.
tldr: This paper proposes a reduction method to lower the condition number bound for Macaulay linear systems, enabling more efficient quantum algorithms for solving Boolean systems and reducing sample complexity in Learning Parities with Structured Noise.
motivation: Quantum linear system algorithms are bottlenecked by the condition number; reducing it would improve their time complexity and enable practical quantum advantage for solving Boolean systems like those in LPSN.
method: The authors introduce a novel reduction for Macaulay linear systems that incorporates a scaling factor to derive a lower bound on the condition number, which reduces the condition number interval and optimizes the upper bound on time complexity.
result: The improved quantum algorithm reduces sample complexity and demonstrates concrete reductions in circuit width, depth, and gate count due to the optimized condition number, and shows potential quantum advantage over classical methods in specific parameter regimes.
conclusion: The paper provides a systematic comparison of quantum and classical approaches, indicating that the optimized quantum algorithm can outperform classical counterparts under certain conditions, highlighting the importance of condition number optimization for quantum advantage.

title: Shifting Social Dispositions, Stable Prosocial Traits: A Global Age-Period-Cohort Analysis Of Human Personality
authors: Paul X. Mccarthy, Xian Gong, John A. Johnson, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu, Margaret L. Kern, Jean M. Twenge
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generational stereotypes are widespread, but they often rely on anecdotes, and it remains challenging to disentangle true birth-cohort differences from the universal effects of ageing and historical periods. Using a statistical approach that separates effects of age, calendar time, and cohort, we analyzed Big Five personality data (five broad dimensions of personality) from N=773,714 individuals assessed across 30 years. Traits that shape social interaction diverged between generations, whereas a prosocial core comprising morality, discipline, and emotional awareness was stable across cohorts. Generation Z (born between 1995 and 2012) showed lower excitement seeking and gregariousness alongside higher self-consciousness and anxiety. These findings suggest that cohort change is selective rather than global: the dispositions through which people engage with the social world may be adapting to contemporary cultural conditions, while core prosocial tendencies remain stable across generations.
tldr: This paper analyzes Big Five personality data from over 770,000 individuals to separate age, period, and cohort effects, finding that social dispositions differ across generations while core prosocial traits remain stable.
motivation: Generational stereotypes are often anecdotal, and disentangling true birth-cohort differences from ageing and historical periods is challenging. The authors aim to provide a rigorous statistical analysis of cohort effects on personality.
method: The study applies an age-period-cohort (APC) statistical approach to a large longitudinal dataset of N=773,714 individuals assessed over 30 years, using Big Five personality measures to separate effects of age, calendar time, and birth cohort.
result: Traits shaping social interaction diverged across generations, with Generation Z showing lower excitement seeking and gregariousness but higher self-consciousness and anxiety, while a prosocial core (morality, discipline, emotional awareness) remained stable.
conclusion: Cohort change in personality is selective rather than global, suggesting that social dispositions adapt to contemporary cultural conditions while core prosocial tendencies persist.

title: How Quantum Is The Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- And Noise-Aware Benchmark And Attribution Audit Of Quantum Machine Learning For Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Shahid Munir Shah, Asher Ali, Hamzah Siddiqui
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) for network intrusion detection (NIDS) is routinely reported to reach near-perfect accuracy, yet the most rigorous studies find that well-tuned classical models remain competitive, and that apparent quantum gains may be artefacts of classical dimensionality reduction and implicit regularisation rather than genuine quantum effects. We ask not whether a quantum model can post a high accuracy, but how quantum the advantage really is. We present a unified, reproducible QML-IDS benchmark evaluating hybrid variational quantum circuits and quantum-kernel SVMs against five honestly-tuned classical baselines across four standard NIDS datasets (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, CICIDS2017, NF-ToN-IoT-v2) under one leakage-controlled protocol, with an equal-budget feature view, imbalance- and calibration-aware metrics with significance testing, and a simulated NISQ noise sweep. We introduce a quantum-attribution audit (parameter-matched classical controls, a random-feature kernel, and a regularisation sweep) that quantifies how much of any gain is genuinely attributable to the quantum component. Tuned classical models (Random Forest, XGBoost) match or exceed the quantum models on aggregate detection on every dataset, and the audit attributes this to classical preprocessing and regularisation rather than quantum effects. Two advantages survive false-discovery-rate correction: the quantum-kernel SVM out-ranks its direct classical surrogate (a random-feature kernel) on AUPRC and ROC-AUC, and a small four-qubit hybrid out-detects the best classical baseline at the 1% false-positive operating point on the distribution-shifted NSL-KDD task (p = 0.005, BH q = 0.030). Code, seeds, and splits are released; our contribution stands whether quantum wins, ties, or loses.
tldr: A benchmark and attribution audit of quantum machine learning for network intrusion detection, finding that classical models match or surpass QML and quantum advantage is often not genuine.
motivation: Many QML-IDS studies report high accuracy, but rigorous comparisons show classical models remain competitive; thus, the paper asks whether quantum advantage is real.
method: They present a unified reproducible benchmark with hybrid variational quantum circuits and quantum-kernel SVMs against classical baselines on four datasets, using controlled protocols, calibration-aware metrics, significance testing, and a noise sweep, plus a quantum-attribution audit.
result: Tuned classical models match or exceed quantum models on aggregate detection; two quantum advantages survive false-discovery-rate correction: quantum-kernel SVM outperforms its surrogate on AUPRC/ROC-AUC, and a small four-qubit hybrid performs better at 1% FPR on NSL-KDD.
conclusion: Most apparent quantum gains are attributable to classical preprocessing and regularization, not quantum effects, but some genuine quantum advantages exist after correction.

title: Grant-Making Under Uncertainty
authors: Daniel L. Goroff
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theory of Decision-making under uncertainty as it applies to NIH grant-making generally and to NIH research plans concerning the science of science in particular.
tldr: The paper examines decision-making under uncertainty in the context of NIH grant allocation and research planning.
motivation: To improve grant-making processes and research planning by applying decision theory under uncertainty.
method: The abstract suggests a theoretical analysis of decision-making frameworks applied to NIH grant-making.
result: The paper likely provides insights or recommendations for better grant decisions under uncertainty.
conclusion: It highlights the importance of considering uncertainty in science policy and funding decisions.

title: Probing The Electroweak Structure Of Nuclei With Rare Atoms And Molecules
authors: Silviu-Marian Udrescu, Antoine Belley, Jason D. Holt, Gilad Perez, Ronald F. Garcia Ruiz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precision experiments of atoms and molecules have become a powerful probe of the electroweak structure of atomic nuclei and of physics beyond the Standard Model. We review how the interaction between a nucleus and its surrounding bound electrons can be exploited to precisely measure the electromagnetic, parity-violating, and CP-violating properties of nuclei and their fundamental constituents. We focus on rare, unstable isotopes, surveying the experimental techniques and facilities developed in recent years that have extended these measurements to the most exotic regions of the nuclear chart. Recent advances in the precision control and interrogation of single molecules, together with direct laser excitation of nuclear transitions, are opening new frontiers in nuclear and particle physics. At the same time, progress in nuclear theory, machine learning, and high-performance computing is strengthening the connection between our microscopic description of nature and laboratory observables. In many cases, the precision with which nuclear and particle physics properties can be extracted is now limited not by experiment, but by the molecular, atomic, or nuclear theory required to interpret the measurements. This challenge presents a major opportunity for combined theoretical and experimental advances that will enable future discoveries.
tldr: This paper reviews precision measurements of electroweak and CP-violating properties of rare isotopes using atomic and molecular spectroscopy, aiming to probe nuclear structure and physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore nuclear electroweak structure and search for new physics beyond the Standard Model using precision atomic/molecular experiments.
method: It surveys experimental techniques for rare isotope spectroscopy, molecular control, and laser excitation of nuclear transitions, along with theoretical progress in nuclear theory and machine learning.
result: The paper highlights that theoretical limitations now often restrict extraction of nuclear properties, presenting opportunities for combined experimental and theoretical advances.
conclusion: Future discoveries will require coordinated improvements in atomic, molecular, and nuclear theory to match experimental precision.

title: Ultra-broadband Integrated Optical Parametric Amplifier For Quantum Sensing
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Tushar Sanjay Karnik, Chun-Ho Lee, Kiyoung Ko, Xinyi Ren, Ian Christen, Reshma Kopparapu, Clayton Cheung, Kiwon Kwon, Kamila Kunes, Zaijun Chen, Mengjie Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) facilitates efficient signal generation and nonlinear and quantum interactions, the realization of optical parametric amplification (OPA) that can provide simultaneous ultra-broadband and high-gain operation in an integrated chip continues to pose a challenge. Here we demonstrate continuous-wave-pumped OPA in an X-cut MgO-doped, dispersion-engineered, and adaptively-poled TFLN waveguide of 1.6 cm length, achieving a flat-top profile covering a 450 nm-wide optical wavelength window, corresponding to a 3-dB gain bandwidth of about 56 THz. Among reported TFLN platforms, our device exhibits the broadest 3-dB gain bandwidth. The same device can be pumped either directly at visible wavelengths through second-order x(2) interactions or in the telecom band through cascaded x(2) processes, the latter eliminating the need for a high-power visible pump laser. We achieve maximum gains of 8.87 +- 0.39 dB and 10.79 +- 0.43 dB at on-chip pump powers of 74 mW and 170 mW for the direct and cascaded schemes, respectively. We further directly probe OPA gain across the 1650-1900 nm wavelength range, where experimental gain measurements have remained scarce. With a normalized on-chip gain of 1.21 dB per W per mm, our device sets a new benchmark among reported cascaded x(2) nonlinear processes. This work advances the realization of integrated optical parametric amplifiers, offering high efficiency, robust gain, ultra-broadband bandwidth, and continuous-wave operation, thereby enabling new capabilities for next-generation quantum sensing and photonic systems.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an ultra-broadband integrated optical parametric amplifier on thin-film lithium niobate with record bandwidth and gain, targeting quantum sensing applications.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of achieving simultaneous ultra-broadband and high-gain operation in integrated optical parametric amplifiers for quantum sensing and photonic systems.
method: The authors use a dispersion-engineered, adaptively-poled X-cut MgO-doped TFLN waveguide, pumped either directly via second-order nonlinearity or through cascaded processes, and measure gain across a wide wavelength range.
result: They achieve a flat-top gain profile spanning 450 nm (3-dB bandwidth ~56 THz), with maximum gains of 8.87 dB and 10.79 dB for direct and cascaded schemes, and a record normalized on-chip gain of 1.21 dB/W/mm.
conclusion: This work sets a new benchmark for integrated optical parametric amplifiers, offering high efficiency, broad bandwidth, and continuous-wave operation, thus enabling next-generation quantum sensing and photonic systems.

title: Bayesian Optimization For Practical H2 Sensors: Inverse Design Of Pd-based Plasmonic Metasurfaces
authors: Pernilla Ekborg-Tanner, Athanasios Theodoridis, Joachim Fritzsche, Christoph Langhammer, Andrea Baldi, Paul Erhart
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hydrogen detection is becoming increasingly important as its use grows across energy and industrial systems. Optical sensing platforms based on palladium (Pd) nanoparticles are attractive for this task because hydrogen uptake directly alters their plasmonic response. Organizing such nanoparticles into periodic two-dimensional arrays, known as metasurfaces, further enhances their optical response through collective resonances. However, the large design space presented by chemical composition, nanoparticle geometry, and array structure calls for systematic approaches for optimizing complex nanoalloy metasurface geometries. Here, we develop an inverse-design framework based on Bayesian optimization that couples first-principles dielectric functions with electromagnetic simulations to identify high-performance PdAu nanodisk arrays for hydrogen sensing in the 1 to 100 mbar range where the flammability of H2 becomes a concern. We use our approach to search a five-dimensional design space, comprising nanodisk height and radius, array pitch, polymer coating thickness, and Au fraction in order to maximize the H-induced change in extinction at a single wavelength of choice. The results show that integrating first-principles optical models with data-efficient optimization yields experimentally feasible nanoparticle metasurfaces tailored for targeted hydrogen pressures, while providing a pathway to future multiobjective sensor design. They also reveal remaining gaps in the modeling methodologies that still limit the quantitative reliability of the approach.
tldr: This paper develops a Bayesian optimization framework to inverse-design PdAu nanodisk metasurfaces for hydrogen sensing.
motivation: Hydrogen detection is critical due to its widespread use, and Pd-based plasmonic sensors have a large design space needing systematic optimization.
method: Couples first-principles dielectric functions with electromagnetic simulations, and uses Bayesian optimization to search a five-dimensional design space (nanodisk height, radius, array pitch, polymer coating thickness, Au fraction).
result: Identifies high-performance PdAu nanodisk arrays for hydrogen sensing in the 1-100 mbar range, maximizing H-induced extinction change at a single wavelength.
conclusion: The approach yields experimentally feasible metasurfaces and provides a pathway to multiobjective sensor design, but reveals gaps in modeling methodologies for quantitative reliability.

title: Variational Quantum Algorithms For Hyperelasticity: Incorporating Nonlinear Constitutive Behavior
authors: Caglar Oskay Uditnarayan Kouskiya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper extends a recently proposed Variational Quantum Algorithm framework for nonlinear elasticity to a broader class of constitutive nonlinearities involving rational powers of the stretch. One-dimensional incompressible Ogden and Mooney-Rivlin models are employed as representative examples to demonstrate the proposed methodology. Nonlinear constitutive terms are transformed into forms compatible with the available quantum algorithmic primitives through the introduction of auxiliary variables and penalty constraints, yielding approximate solutions via a Variational Quantum Algorithm. An iterative correction strategy based on a sequence of Variational Quantum Algorithms is then introduced to improve solution accuracy. A Numerical example demonstrates the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper extends a variational quantum algorithm framework to solve hyperelasticity problems with nonlinear constitutive models using auxiliary variables and penalty constraints.
motivation: To apply variational quantum algorithms to nonlinear elasticity problems, specifically for constitutive models like Ogden and Mooney-Rivlin, which have rational powers of stretch.
method: The nonlinear constitutive terms are transformed into forms compatible with quantum algorithms by introducing auxiliary variables and penalty constraints, and an iterative correction strategy using a sequence of variational quantum algorithms is used to improve accuracy.
result: A numerical example demonstrates the proposed approach, but the paper appears to be a proof-of-concept without extensive benchmarking or clear advantages over classical methods.
conclusion: The work is an exploration of quantum algorithms for computational mechanics, but it does not directly contribute to the listed research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Unified Strong-Field Dynamics Simulations From Atoms To Heterostructures
authors: Amelle Za\"ir Zakaria Dahbi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present , a high-performance open-source framework for strong-field quantum dynamics in atomic, molecular, and semiconductor effective-mass systems. The core engine implements a weak-form Galerkin discretisation of the Hermitian BenDaniel-Duke operator, [MATH], on geometry-adapted B-spline meshes, supporting arbitrary potentials and customisable laser configurations in one to three dimensions.
