We also provide an iterative refinement procedure for the approximation solution that, in our experiments, yields near-optimal results while retaining a substantial speed advantage over our solver for the optimal solution.
tldr: Introduces entropy-constrained adaptive stochastic quantization to minimize MSE under an entropy budget and unbiasedness, with efficient algorithms.
motivation: Existing unbiased quantization methods ignore the subsequent lossless entropy encoding, leaving potential accuracy improvements unexplored.
method: Formulates the ECASQ problem and provides an optimal dynamic program with O(d·s) time and space, plus a GPU-friendly approximate DP that guarantees solution quality within one bit of entropy per entry.
result: The approximate algorithm achieves near-optimal results in experiments with substantial speed advantages over the exact solver.
conclusion: The proposed method improves quantization accuracy under entropy constraints while remaining computationally practical.

title: Redakto - The Incognito Tab For LLMs
authors: Saurav Kumar Saha, Tom R\"ohr, Felix Bie{\ss}mann
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are being increasingly used in everyday applications. A major challenge in the context of LLMs or Artificial Intelligence (AI) in general is to ensure privacy when using them, meaning that personally identifiable information (PII) is removed from any text that enters an LLM. These challenges have become more urgent with novel EU legislation. Uncertainty around LLM usage with respect to privacy concerns in EU countries can be a major blocker for the speed of innovation and transfer from research to applications. Here we present , a tool that can be used for anonymizing text prior to feeding it to an LLM or other downstream text processing. We provide state-of-the-art functionalities for both redaction of PII but also when used for pseudonymization. These functionalities are exposed such that they can easily be used by end-users, through the Redakto web application, and by developers and researchers, via REST APIs and model context protocol (MCP) hooks. The implementation is fully open source, requires modest compute resources, and can be readily deployed on local hardware. In contrast to prior work and in order to better assess the quality of the anonymized texts, we conduct extensive empirical evaluations on textual data from legal and medical domain with respect to both privacy and utility of the redacted texts. Our empirical results demonstrate that the texts anonymized with different redaction strategies achieve utility scores on par with the original texts, suggesting that anonymization with Redakto can be used for LLM tasks without substantial negative impact for the tasks we explored.
tldr: This paper presents Redakto, an open-source tool for anonymizing text before feeding it to LLMs, with empirical evaluations on legal and medical domains.
motivation: Privacy concerns, especially EU legislation, hinder LLM adoption; anonymizing PII before model input is crucial.
method: Develops a tool with redaction and pseudonymization functionalities, exposed via web app, REST APIs, and MCP hooks; evaluates utility and privacy on legal and medical text.
result: Anonymized texts achieve utility scores on par with originals for the tasks explored.
conclusion: Redakto can effectively anonymize data for LLM tasks without substantial performance loss, supporting privacy-compliant use.

title: A Comprehensive Review Of Large Language Models For Nanophotonics: From Surrogate Modeling To Autonomous Design
authors: Huanshu Zhang, Kegeng Tang, Lei Kang, Sawyer D. Campbell, Zihao Wang, Douglas H. Werner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces have revolutionized the development of photonic devices by enabling unprecedented precision in light manipulation. However, their design processes are often constrained by computationally expensive simulations and complex high-dimensional design spaces. Although deep learning has accelerated the design process by serving as a surrogate model, it remains constrained by task-specific architectures and lacks universal reasoning capabilities. This review surveys how Large Language Models (LLMs) are adding semantic interfaces, code generation, and tool orchestration to established numerical nanophotonic workflows. We first outline the development from classical neural networks to transformer-based models and their applications in nanophotonic design. We then review the emergence of LLM-related methods in nanophotonics and organize them into two operational modes: surrogate models that treat structure-spectrum mapping as a language task, and agentic systems that have been demonstrated to generate code, orchestrate selected simulation steps, and support closed-loop optimization. Furthermore, to identify future cross-disciplinary opportunities, we briefly explore applications of LLMs in research fields such as materials science and wireless communications. This review concludes by looking ahead to the next generation of multimodal foundation models with physical perception capabilities. In this vision, artificial intelligence is evolving from passive tools into active collaborators, participating in autonomous scientific discovery.
tldr: This review surveys the application of large language models (LLMs) to nanophotonic device design, covering their roles as surrogate models and agentic systems.
motivation: Nanophotonic design is hindered by expensive simulations and complex design spaces, and conventional deep learning lacks universal reasoning. LLMs offer semantic interfaces, code generation, and tool orchestration to enhance design workflows.
method: The review traces the evolution from classical neural networks to transformer-based models, categorizes LLM applications into surrogate modeling (structure-spectrum mapping as language tasks) and agentic systems that generate code and orchestrate simulations, and explores cross-disciplinary extensions.
result: The paper summarizes current LLM-based methods in nanophotonics, including closed-loop optimization and autonomous design, and identifies future opportunities in materials science and wireless communications.
conclusion: LLMs are evolving from passive tools to active collaborators, potentially enabling autonomous scientific discovery with multimodal foundation models that possess physical perception.

title: Second-Order Asymptotics For The Gaussian Multiple-Access Channel At Corner Points
authors: Vincent Y. F. Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish exact second-order coding rate regions at the two corner points of the capacity region of the two-user Gaussian multiple-access channel. For any average error probability [MATH], we characterize the [MATH]-scale fluctuations of achievable rates around each corner point, proving a converse that matches the previously known achievability bound. The proof first extracts a rectangular subcode that preserves the independence of the two transmitted codewords. The Polyanskiy--Verd\'u good-code output distribution theorem then yields log-determinant constraints that induce a spectral decomposition of a trimmed codebook into diffuse and exceptional subspaces. An entropic Brascamp--Lieb projection inequality controls the codeword inner product on the diffuse subspace, while variance-inflated Gaussian output distributions handle the low-dimensional exceptional subspace. Combining these two treatments yields the joint Gaussian limit required for the matching second-order converse.
tldr: This paper derives exact second-order coding rate regions at the corner points of the two-user Gaussian multiple-access channel capacity region, matching achievability with a converse bound.
motivation: The paper aims to characterize the fine-grained (second-order) asymptotic behavior of achievable rates for the Gaussian multiple-access channel, which is a classical information theory problem not connected to quantum information.
method: The proof uses a rectangular subcode preserving independence, Polyanskiy-Verdú good-code output distribution theorem, spectral decomposition of the codebook, Brascamp-Lieb projection inequality, and variance-inflated Gaussian output distributions.
result: It establishes the exact second-order rate fluctuations around each corner point for any average error probability, confirming that the previously known achievability bound is tight.
conclusion: This is a significant contribution to classical multi-user information theory, but it lies entirely outside the user's quantum-focused research directions.

title: Quantum Processes Under Epistemic Constraints
authors: Varun Immanuel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This doctoral dissertation on the foundations of quantum theory isolates and then formalizes a physically relevant concept that I have called "Epistemic Constraint." Here, epistemic constraints are the definite, intersubjectively agreeable, ordinary-language conditions under which experiments are described. The usual formulation of the quantum measurement problem, which I call the Schrodingerian measurement problem, has the structure of an anomaly: if we take quantum theory at face value, we expect no definite values, and yet we see definite values in experiments. The responses to this problem have been either to solve it or to dissolve it. These responses, which have taken the form of interpretation, modification, or reconstruction of quantum mechanics, seek either to derive (conceptually or mathematically) epistemic constraints from within quantum mechanics or suitable modifications of it, as is the case with certain interpretations and modifications, or to posit the epistemic constraint, or parts of it, as a primitive assumption with the goal of deriving quantum mechanics, as is the case in some reconstruction programs. In contrast to the Schrodingerian measurement problem, which had the structure of an anomaly, this dissertation develops the Bohrian Program, which (for lack of a better comparison) has a structure similar to the problem historically associated with Euclid's fifth postulate. It seeks to keep epistemic constraints as primitive in an onto-epistemic sense. It then seeks new physical conclusions from the joint consideration of quantum mechanics and epistemic constraints, without seeking to derive one from the other. Among other results, this leads to a notion of the probability of instantiability of the Born Rule that specifies when to apply the Born Rule and when to apply a unitary transformation to a quantum state.
tldr: This dissertation formalizes epistemic constraints and proposes the Bohrian Program to address the measurement problem, introducing a notion of probability of instantiability of the Born Rule.
motivation: The usual formulation of the quantum measurement problem is an anomaly; the dissertation aims to keep epistemic constraints primitive rather than deriving them from quantum mechanics.
method: The dissertation develops the Bohrian Program by jointly considering quantum mechanics and epistemic constraints, without deriving one from the other, and introduces a new concept of probability of instantiability of the Born Rule.
result: It specifies when to apply the Born Rule versus unitary evolution, offering new physical conclusions.
conclusion: The approach suggests that epistemic constraints should be treated as primitive, leading to a novel resolution of the measurement problem.

title: Embedding Paired Free-Fermion Gaussian States Into Gutzwiller-Projected Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer Wave Functions
authors: Ryui Kaneko
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gutzwiller-projected Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) wave functions of Abrikosov fermions are widely used to describe quantum many-body states. Taking the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model as an example, we exactly embed any even-parity spinless fermionic Gaussian state representable as a paired exponential in the chosen particle basis into a projected BCS state of spinful Abrikosov fermions. The construction provides controlled initial states for variational Monte Carlo studies of nonintegrable models.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to exactly represent paired free-fermion Gaussian states as Gutzwiller-projected BCS wave functions for the transverse-field Ising model, providing controlled variational initial states.
motivation: To improve variational Monte Carlo simulations of nonintegrable quantum many-body models by constructing accurate initial states.
method: The authors explicitly embed any even-parity spinless fermionic Gaussian state represented as a paired exponential into a projected BCS state of spinful Abrikosov fermions, using the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model as a concrete example.
result: The construction guarantees exact equivalence, enabling controlled starting points for variational Monte Carlo studies.
conclusion: The approach offers a systematic way to generate initial states for nonintegrable models, potentially enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of variational simulations.

title: A Compact Low-frequency Optomechanical Triaxial Inertial Sensor
authors: Daniel George, Jose D. Hernandez Rivero, Moritz Mehmet, Ramses Miranda Espino, Xiangyu Guo, Andrea Nelson, Jose Sanjuan, Felipe Guzman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triaxial optomechanical accelerometers offer compact, ground-testable alternatives to electrostatic sensors for satellite geodesy, seismometry, and various other applications. We demonstrate a low-CSWaP triaxial sensor using monolithic fused-silica resonators with dual heterodyne interferometric readout. The X axis reaches a 60~pico-g/[MATH] readout noise floor, and the in-plane axes resolve ambient seismic ground motion in agreement with a co-located commercial seismometer from 4~mHz to 8~Hz. The Z axis exhibits higher noise under [MATH] loading due to gravity-induced geometric stiffening (44.45~Hz versus 11.07~Hz in a 0g-equivalent configuration), with measurements indicating in-orbit performance on par with the in-plane sensors. These results support the feasibility of triaxial optomechanical accelerometry for space missions and ground-based applications.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a compact triaxial optomechanical accelerometer with low noise floor for space and ground applications.
motivation: To provide compact, ground-testable alternatives to electrostatic sensors for satellite geodesy and seismometry.
method: Uses monolithic fused-silica resonators with dual heterodyne interferometric readout to measure acceleration along three axes.
result: Achieves 60 pico-g/√Hz noise floor on the X axis, resolves seismic ground motion from 4 mHz to 8 Hz matching a commercial seismometer; the Z axis has higher noise due to gravity stiffening but in-orbit performance is comparable.
conclusion: The feasibility of triaxial optomechanical accelerometry for space missions and ground-based applications is supported.

title: Toward Topology-Optimized Foundry PDKs: A Seeded Design Framework For Multimode Interferometers
authors: Jacob M. Hiesener, Archana Kaushalram, Joshua J. Wong, Robert P. Pesch, Stephen E. Ralph
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an end-to-end design methodology for multimode interferometer (MMI)-based photonic devices that combines parameter optimization (PO) on analytical models with seeded topology optimization (TO) to maximize performance while preserving foundry design-rule compliance. A PO seed device is further refined via seeded TO, accessing a larger design space than analytical or parameterized methods alone can reach. We validate this pipeline on a 1x2 splitter, a TE modal multiplexer, and a polarization splitter, fabricating and measuring the first two on a commercial foundry process. Seeded TO reduces the measured insertion loss of the 1x2 splitter from 0.20 to 0.14 dB and improves TE00 transmission of the modal multiplexer from -2.79 to -1.01 dB over O-band. Applying this pipeline to a commercial foundry process design kit (PDK)-provided 1x2 and 2x2 splitter improves simulated transmission and tightens the 2x2 splitting ratio from 0.524 to 0.506, along with improved fabrication robustness, offering a practical, foundry-validated route toward incorporating TO-designed components into commercial PDKs.
tldr: A design framework for multimode interferometers that combines parameter optimization and seeded topology optimization to improve performance and foundry compliance.
motivation: To improve the design of photonic devices like MMIs by leveraging topology optimization while ensuring they meet foundry design rules.
method: Combines parameter optimization on analytical models with seeded topology optimization, and validates on fabricated devices.
result: Seeded TO reduces insertion loss for a 1x2 splitter and improves transmission for a modal multiplexer; also improves simulated performance of foundry PDK components.
conclusion: This pipeline offers a practical route for incorporating topology-optimized components into commercial PDKs.

title: Directional Hydrogen Migration In Acetonitrile Dication In Asymmetric Ultrashort Intense Laser Fields
authors: Sato Miyasaka, Yuki Ono, Hiroka Hasegawa, Runa Kuroda, Akitaka Matsuda, Akiyoshi Hishikawa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate intramolecular hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dication in phase-controlled [MATH]-[MATH] intense laser fields (800 and 400 nm, 3.3[MATH]10[MATH] W/cm[MATH]) using three-dimensional coincidence ion momentum imaging. The two-body Coulomb explosion pathway, CH[MATH]CN[MATH] [MATH] CH[MATH] + CN[MATH], exhibits a clear phase-dependent fragment asymmetry along the laser polarization direction, showing that the tunnel ionization preferentially prepares the acetonitrile dication with the methyl group pointing toward the smaller amplitude side of the laser electric fields. The Coulomb explosion pathway occurring after the migration of a single hydrogen atom, CH[MATH]CN[MATH] [MATH] CH[MATH] + HCN[MATH], shows a pronounced reduction in the fragment asymmetry. A clear deuteration effect observed for the asymmetry of the hydrogen-migration pathway suggests that the two-color asymmetric laser field has a significant impact on directionality of intramolecular hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dication.
tldr: This paper studies directional hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dications under asymmetric two-color intense laser fields, using coincidence ion momentum imaging.
motivation: To understand how asymmetric laser fields control intramolecular hydrogen migration, a key process in laser-induced chemistry.
method: Using three-dimensional coincidence ion momentum imaging, they measure Coulomb explosion pathways of acetonitrile dications produced by phase-controlled 800 nm + 400 nm intense laser fields, analyzing fragment asymmetries and deuteration effects.
result: They observe phase-dependent fragment asymmetry for the CH3CN2+ -> CH3+ + CN+ channel, and a reduced asymmetry for the hydrogen migration pathway CH3CN2+ -> CH2+ + HCN+, with a clear deuteration effect.
conclusion: The asymmetric two-color laser field influences the directionality of intramolecular hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dications, providing insights into laser control of molecular dynamics.

title: Branching (Almost) Everywhere And All At Once
authors: Alyssa Ney
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is sometimes said that a reason to prefer Everettian quantum mechanics is that it allows one to avoid the kind of spooky action at a distance that is a consequence of quantum entanglement according to other approaches. There is a straightforward argument to show EQM has this virtue, however some advocates argue that this requires we see branching as a local causal process. I explain this reasoning and then show why, given the way Everettians standardly conceive of worlds and branching as emergent phenomena, branching need not be viewed as a causal process for EQM to be relativistically local. Forthcoming in Local Quantum Mechanics, OUP 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the locality of branching in Everettian quantum mechanics, arguing that branching need not be viewed as a causal process for the theory to maintain relativistic locality.
motivation: To address the claim that Everettian quantum mechanics avoids spooky action at a distance, and to clarify the role of branching as an emergent phenomenon.
method: Conceptual analysis and argumentation, drawing on standard Everettian interpretations of worlds and branching as emergent.
result: The paper shows that branching need not be a causal process for EQM to be relativistically local, contrary to some advocates' claims.
conclusion: Everettian quantum mechanics can maintain locality without treating branching as a causal process, based on the emergent nature of worlds.

title: Optimal Loss Allocation In A Mean-Field Model Of Systemic Risk
authors: Qinxin Yan Yucheng Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a systemic-risk control problem in which a central planner allocates losses generated by bank defaults across the surviving institutions. Banks are modeled through their distances to default, evolving as absorbed Brownian motions with downward jumps induced by redistributed default losses. Unlike bailout models, the planner cannot inject external capital or reduce the aggregate loss, and the only admissible intervention is to decide how each endogenous loss is assigned among solvent banks. The objective is to maximize terminal system health, including survival mass as a leading special case and, more generally, increasing concave welfare functionals of the terminal distribution. Our main result identifies an optimal allocation rule with a simple economic interpretation: losses should be concentrated on the currently healthiest institutions. In discrete time, this rule takes the form of a cutoff or taxing-the-richest policy, which reduces banks above an endogenous threshold down to that threshold while leaving weaker banks untouched. We prove convergence of the time-discretized mean-field control problem as the allocation time step tends to zero and characterize the limiting problem as a singular mean-field control problem. The optimally controlled law is described by a reflected free-boundary formulation, in which the cutoff becomes the moving upper edge of the support, and the associated value function satisfies a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on Wasserstein space. Finally, we formulate the corresponding finite-particle control problem and show, under suitable assumptions, that the cutoff-controlled particle system converges to the continuous-time mean-field model. This provides a finite-system foundation for the optimal mean-field loss-allocation rule.
tldr: The paper studies optimal loss allocation in a systemic risk model using mean-field control, focusing on concentrating losses on the healthiest banks.
motivation: To find an optimal strategy for a central planner to allocate losses from bank defaults among surviving institutions without external capital, maximizing terminal system health.
method: Models banks' distances to default as absorbed Brownian motions with jumps, formulates a mean-field control problem, and derives a cutoff (tax-the-richest) policy in discrete time, then proves convergence to a continuous-time singular mean-field control problem.
result: Identifies an optimal allocation rule that concentrates losses on the healthiest institutions, with a reflected free-boundary characterization and convergence of particle systems.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous mean-field foundation for optimal loss allocation in systemic risk, suggesting that concentrating losses on healthier banks is optimal.

title: Formal Safety Verification For Nonlinear Systems With Generative Barrier Certificate
authors: Hanrui Zhao Mengxin Ren
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety verification is a fundamental problem in control theory. Barrier certificates (BCs) provide a powerful formal mechanism, yet deriving BCs is computationally intensive. This paper introduces a generative framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to synthesize BCs through reasoning. Based on the classical Sum-of-Squares (SOS) approach, we train a domain-specific LLM capable of generating high-quality BC candidates for nonlinear systems. Then, the LLM-generated BCs transform the intractable Bilinear Matrix Inequality (BMI) solving problems into convex Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) feasibility test, significantly improving efficiency while preserving correctness. Experimental results show that our generative method achieves several orders of magnitude speedup over traditional numerical BC approaches and, perhaps surprisingly, surpasses the state-of-the-art dedicated neural BC model. These findings mark a substantive step toward integrating generative AI with formal safety verification for dynamical systems.
tldr: This paper introduces a generative approach using large language models to synthesize barrier certificates for formal safety verification of nonlinear systems, significantly improving efficiency.
motivation: Barrier certificates are powerful for safety verification but computationally intensive to derive.
method: The authors train a domain-specific LLM to generate barrier certificate candidates, converting BMI problems into LMI feasibility tests.
result: The generative method achieves orders of magnitude speedup over traditional numerical approaches and outperforms a state-of-the-art neural barrier certificate model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of integrating generative AI with formal safety verification for dynamical systems.

title: Toward Realistic Energy Forecasting: A Delay-Enhanced Fractional-Order Supply-Demand Model
authors: S. Noeiaghdam S. Naveen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to represent the complex dynamics of contemporary energy systems, a novel fractional-order energy supply-demand model with time delay is presented in this investigation. The fractional model, compared to traditional integer-order models, naturally accommodates for memory and genetic effects, and the incorporation of delay component takes into account unavoidable lags in energy production, transmission, and consumption. To ensure the mathematical rigor of the proposed model, we prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions. We additionally examine into the model's stability within the Ulam-Hyers concept and demonstrate that it is resilient to minor uncertainties and perturbations. To handle fractional derivatives with delay systems, we utilize the Grnwald-Letnikov (GL) discretization scheme, which offers a straightforward and effective method for approximating the solutions. The impact of delay parameters and fractional orders on system behavior is investigated numerically, demonstrating how they shape oscillations, convergence rates, and equilibrium states. According to the results, fractional-order modeling with delay, reinforced by the GL discretization scheme, provides a flexible and realistic framework for examining energy dynamics. This framework gives important insights for long-term policy planning, supply management, and demand forecasting. Additionally, the framework lays the groundwork for upcoming additions that incorporate optimization techniques, stochastic effects, and the integration of renewable energy sources, all of which will further the development of effective and sustainable energy systems. We also discuss three sensitivity analysis scenarios including high demand combined with low supply, high renewable and reduced and imports low demand with high imports which the results show stable and efficient results.
tldr: This paper proposes a fractional-order supply-demand model with time delay for energy forecasting, analyzing stability and sensitivity.
motivation: To capture complex dynamics of energy systems with memory effects and unavoidable time lags in production, transmission, and consumption.
method: Uses fractional-order differential equations with delay, proves existence/uniqueness, Ulam-Hyers stability, employs Grünwald-Letnikov discretization, and conducts numerical simulations including sensitivity analysis.
result: The model demonstrates stable and efficient behavior under various demand-supply scenarios, with fractional order and delay shaping oscillations and convergence.
conclusion: Provides a flexible and realistic framework for energy dynamics and forecasting, with potential extensions to optimization, stochastic effects, and renewable integration.

title: Learning The Center And Radius Of Wasserstein Ambiguity Sets For Data-Driven Decision Making
authors: Junjie Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO) is commonly built around the empirical distribution, with the ambiguity radius selected from a concentration bound. Although this construction provides useful statistical guarantees, it can be conservative and does not fully exploit predictive information about the underlying distribution or the difficulty of a particular decision problem. We develop a more flexible framework in which a predictive model determines the nominal distribution and a separate model estimates a data-dependent radius. The key requirement is not that the ambiguity set be centered at the empirical distribution, but that it contain the unknown data-generating distribution with the desired probability. We establish finite-sample guarantees and asymptotic consistency for arbitrary learned centers, derive tractable reformulations for non-uniform discrete predictive distributions, separate predictive-model and scenario-discretization errors, and prove stability under simultaneous perturbations of the center and radius. We further characterize the oracle conditional-quantile radius as the smallest conditionally valid rule and introduce a split-conformal procedure for finite-sample marginal calibration. Experiments on newsvendor problems, synthetic portfolios, distribution shifts, and real financial data show that learned and calibrated ambiguity sets can improve reliability, but do not automatically yield smaller radii or better decisions. Overall, the proposed framework treats calibration as a practical mechanism for reliable decision making rather than a universal guarantee of improved optimization performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a flexible framework for Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization with learned centers and data-dependent radii, providing statistical guarantees and calibration methods.
motivation: Traditional Wasserstein DRO relies on the empirical distribution and conservative concentration bounds, which can be suboptimal and ignores predictive information. The authors aim to improve reliability by learning the center and radius from data.
method: The method uses predictive models to determine the nominal distribution and a separate model for the radius, establishes finite-sample and asymptotic guarantees for arbitrary centers, and introduces a split-conformal procedure for marginal calibration.
result: Experiments on newsvendor, synthetic portfolios, distribution shifts, and financial data show that learned and calibrated ambiguity sets can enhance reliability but do not always lead to smaller radii or better decisions.
conclusion: The framework positions calibration as a practical tool for reliable decision making rather than a guaranteed way to improve optimization performance.

motivation: The authors aim to extend known results about elementary operators by considering a class where one operator is hyponormal and the other normal.

title: Optimizing Energy Efficiency And Grid Stability Via Public Ev Charging Flexibility
authors: Marek Miltner, Artem Bryksa, Ond\v{r}ej \v{s}togl, Daniel Va\v{s}ata, Magda Friedjungov\'a, Ram Rajagopal, Old\v{r}ich Star\'y
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study evaluates the potential of electric vehicle (EV) charging flexibility to enhance both energy efficiency and power grid stability. Using real-world data from public charging stations in Prague, we analyze individual and aggregated charging sessions to explore how optimizing charging times can reduce energy waste, minimize grid imbalances, and support the integration of renewable energy. By aligning EV charging with periods of lower grid demand and higher renewable generation, we demonstrate a significant improvement in energy efficiency, reduc ing the need for costly system support and ancillary services. Our findings suggest that cooperation between power distributors and transmission system operators can unlock new opportunities for maintaining grid stability while promoting sustainable energy use in an increasingly uncertain energy landscape.
tldr: This study evaluates the potential of EV charging flexibility to enhance energy efficiency and grid stability using real-world data from Prague.
motivation: To reduce energy waste and grid imbalances, and support renewable energy integration.
method: Analyze individual and aggregated charging sessions from public charging stations, optimizing charging times aligned with low demand and high renewable generation.
result: Significant improvement in energy efficiency, reducing need for costly system support and ancillary services.
conclusion: Cooperation between distributors and TSOs can unlock opportunities for grid stability and sustainable energy.

title: Online Bipartite Matching With Reusable Capacity Under Non-Stationary Rewards
authors: Xi Chen, Shixin Wang, Bingkun Zhou, Yuan Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study online bipartite matching with reusable server capacity and non-stationary rewards. Jobs arrive sequentially, reveal compatible servers, reward rates, and processing durations, and must be accepted or rejected irrevocably. An accepted job occupies one unit of server capacity only during its processing interval, so an assignment may displace an unknown sequence of future jobs. Existing guarantees are typically calibrated by a global reward range, which can become arbitrarily large when rewards drift over a long horizon. We instead impose a locally bounded reward condition: reward rates of jobs that can compete for the same server within a relevant time window differ by at most a factor [MATH]. Under this condition, we develop two BALANCE-type algorithms with time-aware opportunity-cost losses. TS-BAL maximizes cumulative blocking losses over feasible reuse schedules and achieves a competitive ratio of [MATH]. GR-BAL uses a greedy relaxation of this loss and achieves [MATH], matching a lower bound of [MATH] in the leading term. Numerical experiments demonstrate robust performance under substantial global reward drift and favorable finite-capacity performance.
tldr: This paper studies online bipartite matching with reusable capacity under non-stationary rewards and proposes two BALANCE-type algorithms with competitive ratio guarantees.
motivation: Existing algorithms for online matching with reusable capacity rely on global reward range assumptions, which degrade when rewards drift over time. The authors introduce a locally bounded reward condition to overcome this and design algorithms that perform well under non-stationary rewards.
method: They develop two algorithms: TS-BAL, which maximizes cumulative blocking losses over feasible reuse schedules, and GR-BAL, a greedy relaxation. Both incorporate time-aware opportunity-cost losses and are analyzed under a locally bounded reward condition.
result: TS-BAL achieves a competitive ratio of X, and GR-BAL achieves Y, matching a lower bound of Z in the leading term. Numerical experiments show robust performance under substantial reward drift and favorable finite-capacity performance.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms provide improved guarantees for online bipartite matching with reusable capacity under non-stationary rewards by leveraging local reward bounds.

title: Near-MDS Codes Of Lengths Q+6 And Q+7 From Conics In PG(2,q), Q Odd
authors: Sinan Donmez, Atilla Akpinar, Rumi Melih Pelen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near maximum distance separable (NMDS) codes of dimension 3 and length n over the finite field with q elements are equivalent to (n,3)-arcs in PG(2,q). For every odd prime power q we construct, by adding five suitable points to a conic of PG(2,q), a family of [q+6,3,q+3] NMDS codes and determine their weight distributions completely; three distinct weight enumerators occur, governed by two explicit quadratic-character conditions on the parameters. For every odd prime power q, no code of our family is monomially equivalent to a code of the recent [q+6,3,q+3] NMDS family of Fan, Wang and Xu, even where the weight enumerators of the two families coincide: the separating invariant is a triple of geometric data attached to the underlying arc. Extending the configuration by a sixth point on a distinguished external line, we further obtain [q+7,3,q+4] NMDS codes, together with their weight distributions, for every odd prime power q >= 11 (admissible parameters exist for no q <= 9); the existence proof combines exact and Weil-type character sum estimates with a finite computer verification. Our proofs are purely geometric and rest on a simple counting identity for the trisecant lines of a point set obtained by extending a conic. All the codes constructed are optimal locally recoverable codes with locality 2.
tldr: This paper constructs new families of near-MDS codes from conics in PG(2,q) and computes their weight distributions, but it is purely classical coding theory with no connection to quantum information.
motivation: The authors aim to construct new NMDS codes with optimal parameters and determine their weight enumerators, extending recent results by Fan, Wang, and Xu.
method: They use geometric constructions based on conics in PG(2,q), adding points to form arcs, and apply counting identities for trisecant lines along with character sum estimates and computer verification.
result: They construct [q+6,3,q+3] and [q+7,3,q+4] NMDS codes for odd q, provide complete weight distributions, and show their codes are not monomially equivalent to known families.
conclusion: The paper contributes to classical coding theory and locally recoverable codes, but is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Banach's Isometric Conjecture Over The Complex Field
authors: Tomasz Kania Antonio Acuaviva
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We complete Banach's isometric conjecture over the complex field. More precisely, if \(X\) is a complex normed space and, for some \(2\leqslant n<\dim_{\C}X\), all its \(n\)-dimensional complex subspaces are isometric as metric spaces, then the norm is induced by a Hermitian inner product. We also prove the quaternionic counterpart. The central geometric argument first treats real star bodies without convexity or central symmetry; applied to circled complex or quaternionic bodies, it shows that mutually real-linearly equivalent hyperplane sections force the ambient body to be a Hermitian ellipsoid. The proof adapts the bundle-degree mechanism introduced by Lu and Yang for the real case. Finally, we obtain extensions to absolutely homogeneous functions, graded Fr\'echet spaces, metrisable locally convex spaces, and compatible translation-invariant metrics.
tldr: The paper proves Banach's isometric conjecture over the complex and quaternionic fields, characterizing Hermitian inner product spaces via isometric hyperplane sections.
motivation: To complete a classical conjecture in Banach space theory, extending earlier real-case results to complex and quaternionic settings, with implications for the geometric structure of normed spaces.
method: The proof uses a geometric argument on real star bodies without convexity or central symmetry, adapting the bundle-degree mechanism introduced by Lu and Yang for the real case, and extends to absolutely homogeneous functions and certain topological vector spaces.
result: If all n-dimensional complex (or quaternionic) subspaces of a normed space are isometric as metric spaces, then the norm is induced by a Hermitian inner product, provided n is at least 2 and less than the dimension. Extensions to other spaces are also obtained.
conclusion: The conjecture is settled for complex and quaternionic fields, reinforcing the unique role of Hermitian inner product spaces in isometric geometry, though it is far from the stated research directions.

title: Self-supervised In-context Operator Learning For Stochastic Mean-Field Control
authors: Suyi Gao, Mo Zhou, Rongjie Lai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic mean-field control (MFC) provides a fundamental framework for coordinating large populations of interacting agents under uncertainty, with a wide range of applications. Existing numerical and deep-learning methods solve one MFC problem instance at a time and must be re-optimized whenever the task changes. In this work, we formulate stochastic MFC as an operator-learning problem and develop, to the best of our knowledge, the first mesh-free, self-supervised neural operator for stochastic MFC. The main challenge is that the diffusion term in the controlled Fokker--Planck equation precludes deterministic transport-map representations. We address this challenge by combining the probability-flow ODE with an invertible normalizing-flow-based transformer, which recasts the dynamics as a deterministic continuity equation and enables closed-form score evaluation through the exact inverse and analytical log-determinant of the normalizing flow, with [MATH] cost per particle for networks of fixed size. Through transformer-based in-context learning, task prompts, represented by compact distribution parameters or raw particle clouds, condition the transport map, enabling a single pretrained operator to solve unseen tasks in one forward pass. The resulting (NFIST) is trained end-to-end by minimizing the stochastic control objective directly, requiring no precomputed numerical solutions for training. We further prove the consistency of the proposed operator-learning formulation with task-by-task optimization. Numerical experiments on stochastic optimal control, Schr\"odinger bridge, systemic-risk control, and obstacle-avoiding path planning demonstrate effective zero-shot generalization while substantially reducing the computational cost of solving large families of stochastic MFC problems.
tldr: This paper presents a mesh-free, self-supervised neural operator for stochastic mean-field control using normalizing flows and transformer-based in-context learning, enabling zero-shot generalization across tasks.
motivation: Existing numerical and deep-learning methods solve one mean-field control problem at a time, requiring re-optimization when tasks change; the authors aim to develop a single operator that can solve unseen tasks efficiently.
method: The authors formulate stochastic MFC as an operator-learning problem, combining the probability-flow ODE with an invertible normalizing-flow-based transformer to handle the diffusion term, and train the model end-to-end by directly minimizing the stochastic control objective.
result: Numerical experiments on stochastic optimal control, Schrödinger bridge, systemic-risk control, and obstacle-avoiding path planning demonstrate effective zero-shot generalization with substantially reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed NFIST operator provides a single pretrained model that can solve a family of stochastic MFC problems in one forward pass, offering a significant efficiency improvement over instance-by-instance optimization.

title: How Far Are $d$-dimensional Copulas With Uniform $(d-1)$-marginals From (total) Independence?
authors: Damjana Kokol Bukov\v{s}ek, Nik Stopar, Wolfgang Trutschnig
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the family [MATH] of all [MATH]-dimensional copulas whose [MATH]-dimensional marginals are all equal to the [MATH]-dimensional product copula [MATH] and tackle the natural question, `how far away' from the [MATH]-dimensional product copula [MATH] elements in [MATH] can be. We provide definitive answers for both, the uniform metric [MATH] as well as the stronger, conditioning-based metric [MATH]. The established results clearly indicate that the family [MATH] is larger than one might expect.
tldr: This paper measures the maximal distance from independence for d-dimensional copulas with independent (d-1)-marginals under two metrics.
motivation: To understand how much dependence can exist in copulas even when all lower-order marginals are independent.
method: The authors consider the family of d-dimensional copulas with uniform (d-1)-marginals and derive formulas for the maximum distance from the product copula in both the uniform and conditioning-based metrics.
result: They provide definitive answers for the maximal distances in both metrics, showing that the family is larger than previously expected.
conclusion: The results indicate that copulas with independent (d-1)-marginals can still deviate significantly from full independence.

title: Existence And Qualitative Theory For Nonlinear Accretive Evolutions With Carath\'eodory Forcing
authors: Dieter Bothe
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be [MATH]-accretive in a real Banach space [MATH]. Given closed sets [MATH], we develop an existence theory for mild solutions of the constrained problem \[ u'(t)+Au(t)\ni f(t,u(t)), \qquad u(t)\in K_A(t):=K(t)\cap, \] where the forcing is Carath\'eodory on the effective tube [MATH]. Under a linear-growth hypothesis and the corresponding regular- and exceptional-time subtangential conditions, we reduce the problem to a bounded effective tube with a common integrable bound. % A first central result constructs a closed separable resolvent-invariant subspace preserving distances to the moving sets and the subtangential conditions, permitting use of the Scorza--Dragoni property for the reduced forcing. tldr: Develops an existence theory for mild solutions of constrained nonlinear accretive evolution equations with Carathéodory forcing in Banach spaces.
motivation: To address constrained evolution problems with time-dependent constraints and Carathéodory forcing, which arise in reaction-diffusion systems.
method: Uses subtangential conditions, a two-level approximation with current-time selectors, and reduction to bounded effective tubes with common integrable bounds.
result: Establishes well-posedness under locally Lipschitz forcing and derives viability, comparison principles, nonautonomous Lyapunov pairs, periodic solutions, and time-dependent bounds.
conclusion: Provides a general abstract framework for constrained nonlinear evolution equations, with applications to reaction-diffusion systems.

title: Posterior Convergence Without Force Convergence: Resolution-Stable Sampling For Rough Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Xiaomei Yang Zhiliang Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian posteriors can converge under model refinement even when the exact sensitivities used by gradient-based samplers do not. We study this mismatch for discretely scale-invariant rough potentials and its consequences for Metropolized Hamiltonian proposals. For Weierstrass truncations, adjacent classical-force increments grow geometrically in the rough regime, whereas fixed additive quotients converge uniformly and fixed multiplicative quotients converge locally away from the origin. The matched Jackson quotient is distinguished not by convergence alone but by dilation covariance and exact finite closure at the intrinsic scale. Uniform negative-log-likelihood approximation is shown to imply explicit total-variation, Hellinger, and bounded quantity-of-interest convergence, with a Gaussian forward-map criterion for Bayesian inverse problems. At the algorithmic level, measurable kick--drift--kick maps are triangular shears, so exact Metropolis correction does not require differentiability of the proposal field. Local uniform field convergence yields convergence of fixed-length proposals, acceptance functions, and bounded-Lipschitz kernels on common compact sets, while the first classical HMC half-kick has no fixed-step refinement limit. Numerical experiments verify the predicted force-refinement rates, show that posterior stabilization can coexist with severe resolution-dependent retuning of exact-gradient HMC, and demonstrate forward convergence without sensitivity convergence in two-dimensional Darcy flow. The computations are used to assess refinement consistency rather than to claim a universal efficiency ordering among proposal fields.
tldr: This paper studies Bayesian posterior convergence in rough inverse problems despite non-convergent sensitivities, focusing on Metropolized Hamiltonian proposals for discretized scale-invariant potentials.
motivation: To address the mismatch between posterior convergence and force convergence in Bayesian inverse problems with rough potentials, which complicates gradient-based sampling methods.
method: The authors analyze Weierstrass-type truncated potentials, prove convergence guarantees for posterior measures under Gaussian forward maps, and develop measurable kick-drift-kick maps treated as triangular shears, with numerical experiments in Darcy flow.
result: They show that posterior stabilization can occur even when exact-gradient HMC requires severe retuning, and that forward convergence does not imply sensitivity convergence.
conclusion: The work clarifies that posterior accuracy can be achieved without sensitivity convergence, and proposes compatible proposal fields while cautioning against universal efficiency claims.

title: (co)Quasi-irreducible And (co)expanding Random Maps
authors: Pablo G. Barrientos, Isaia Nisoli, Dominique Malicet
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quasi-irreducibility, expansion, and their cotangent duals for random [MATH] (local) diffeomorphisms on compact invariant sets of a Riemannian manifold. Quasi-irreducibility is defined through stationary lifts to the projective tangent bundle: every lift must realize the Furstenberg--Kifer formula for the top Lyapunov exponent. We prove that, for ergodic stationary measures, this is equivalent to the absence of equators, namely non-random invariant subbundles on which the top exponent drops. Under simplicity of the first Lyapunov exponent for every stationary measure, quasi-irreducibility is also equivalent to vertical mostly contraction, contraction on average, a vertical spectral gap, and uniqueness of stationary projective lifts. We then apply these criteria to continuity of the top Lyapunov exponent and to expansion on average. In particular, expansion is characterized by positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent on all non-random invariant subbundles; under quasi-irreducibility, it is equivalent to positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent for every stationary measure. Dual statements hold for coquasi-irreducibility, coequators, coexpansion, and continuity of the bottom Lyapunov exponent. We also describe the interplay between expansion and coexpansion and extend the formalism to Grassmannian bundles, obtaining higher-dimensional versions controlling intermediate sums of Lyapunov exponents.
tldr: This paper studies quasi-irreducibility and expansion of random diffeomorphisms on compact invariant sets, linking these properties to Lyapunov exponents and stationary measures.
motivation: To understand the dynamical behavior of random maps and characterize when their Lyapunov exponents are well-defined and continuous.
method: Uses stationary lifts to the projective tangent bundle, Furstenberg-Kifer formula, and ergodic stationary measures to define and analyze quasi-irreducibility.
result: Proves equivalences between quasi-irreducibility and absence of equators, vertical spectral gaps, and uniqueness of stationary lifts, and applies these to expansion and continuity of Lyapunov exponents.
conclusion: Provides criteria for expansion and coexpansion in random dynamical systems, extending to higher-dimensional bundles and intermediate Lyapunov exponents.

title: Quickest Change Detection In Parametric Models With 1-Bit Measurements
authors: Martina Cardone Liyan Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the quickest change detection from 1-bit quantized observations, where the post-change distribution is a parametric model with unknown parameters and the quantization thresholds are jointly chosen with the detection statistic. We propose an Adaptive-Quantization-Threshold CUSUM (AQuTeCUSUM) algorithm, which estimates the post-change parameter online and adaptively selects the quantization threshold to maximize the induced Kullback-Leibler divergence. Under suitable regularity conditions, we characterize the average run length and worst-case average detection delay of the AQuTe-CUSUM procedure, and show that it is asymptotically optimal in first-order as the average run length goes to infinity. Finally, we assess the performance of AQuTe-CUSUM for two distributions, namely the Gaussian and Poisson.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive quantization threshold CUSUM algorithm for quickest change detection with 1-bit quantized observations, demonstrating asymptotic optimality.
motivation: To handle change detection when data is quantized to 1-bit, which reduces communication or storage, while maintaining detection performance.
method: They design an algorithm that adaptively selects quantization thresholds to maximize the Kullback-Leibler divergence, estimate the post-change parameter online, and use CUSUM.
result: They characterize the average run length and worst-case detection delay, proving first-order asymptotic optimality as the average run length goes to infinity.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for Gaussian and Poisson distributions, showcasing its practical applicability.

title: A Relative Variational Principle For Expanding Iterated Function Systems
authors: Jason Tu Gregory Hemenway
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variational principle is a key tool in the study of invariant measures for chaotic dynamical systems. In recent times, dynamicists have developed techniques in random and nonstationary systems to better model real-world phenomena. Here, we prove a relative variational principle for a class of expanding iterated function systems. In particular, we use a nonstationary Ruelle--Perron--Frobenius theorem to show that the marginal entropy given an ergodic invariant measure on the symbolic base equals the average topological entropy along fibers in the induced skew product.
tldr: A relative variational principle for expanding iterated function systems is proved using nonstationary Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius theory.
motivation: To extend variational principles to random and nonstationary dynamical systems for modeling real-world phenomena.
method: Uses a nonstationary Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius theorem to show that marginal entropy given an ergodic invariant measure on the symbolic base equals the average topological entropy along fibers in the induced skew product.
result: Proves the relative variational principle for a class of expanding iterated function systems.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical result in ergodic theory for nonstationary systems, advancing the understanding of entropy in such settings.

title: Optimization Of The Railcar Assignment Problem Using Zone-based Double Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Joseph Geunes Ruonan Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Railcar switching, or shunting operations decisions play a significant role in the efficient operation of railyard systems, which are in turn critical to the fast and effective movement of goods. In flat yards, switching operations are primarily performed using locomotives to push and pull railcars in order to assemble and disassemble trains. In such settings, railcars with predefined destinations are located across multiple parallel rail tracks, and must be moved, or switched, in order to form desired outbound trains. This study addresses the Railcar Assignment Problem (RAP) in flat yards with an objective of minimizing the total number of switching movements. We present a novel mixed-integer programming (MIP) model for this problem that incorporates practical operational constraints in rail yards, and demonstrate its NP-hardness. To solve large-scale instances, we propose a comprehensive Zone-based Double Deep Q-Network (Zone-DDQN) heuristic method that integrates railway structure, yard-zone decomposition, and a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN). The yard-zone decomposition strategy partitions the yard into multiple parallel yard zones, after which the DDQN is applied to solve the problem within each zone individually and sequentially. Computational experiments across small-, medium-, and large-scale yards were conducted on a series of RAP instances. Average results show that the Zone-DDQN heuristic achieves an average optimality gap of [MATH] across small-scale yard instances. For large-scale yard instances containing more than 150 railcars and 30 tracks, the MIP model was not able to obtain solutions within 24 hours. In contrast, the Zone-DDQN heuristic was able to solve these instances with an average running time of 214.42 seconds.
tldr: This paper addresses the railcar assignment problem in flat yards using a mixed-integer programming model and a zone-based double deep Q-network heuristic to minimize switching movements.
motivation: Efficient railyard operations are critical for goods movement, and the railcar assignment problem is NP-hard, requiring scalable solutions for large instances.
method: The authors formulate an MIP model and propose a Zone-DDQN heuristic that decomposes the yard into zones and solves each zone sequentially using double deep Q-learning.
result: For large-scale instances with over 150 railcars and 30 tracks, the heuristic solves within ~214 seconds on average, while the MIP model cannot find solutions within 24 hours.
conclusion: The zone-based deep reinforcement learning approach offers an effective and efficient solution for large-scale railcar assignment problems, outperforming exact methods.

authors: Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev, Ran Xu, Yunpeng Zhu

title: Verblunsky Coefficients, Cmv Matrices And Numerical Invariants Of Homogeneous Bidisc Submodules
authors: Chao Zu Yufeng Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the principal submodule generated by a polynomial in [MATH]. For homogeneous [MATH], the homogeneous slices of [MATH] admit a weighted OPUC model in which the two wandering vectors are an orthonormal polynomial and its reversal. We show that the associated Verblunsky coefficients determine the singular values of the wandering-projection product and the restricted cross-commutator, as well as the non-zero spectrum of the core operator. Toeplitz-determinant and Mahler-measure identities yield exact Fredholm determinants and Schatten estimates, while [MATH] rules out a uniform Hilbert--Schmidt bound. The same model gives explicit singular values of [MATH] on the homogeneous quotient [MATH]; for [MATH], its squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is asymptotic to [MATH]. For arbitrary polynomial generators, we construct a weighted bivariate model with a doubly Toeplitz, block-banded moment matrix and prove [MATH], relating the core spectrum to the cross-Gram operator between the two edge spaces. We also discuss cyclic-factor obstructions, represent higher numerical invariants by alternating CMV products, and give a quadratic counterexample to their proposed monotonicity.
tldr: This paper studies Verblunsky coefficients and CMV matrices for homogeneous bidisc submodules, deriving numerical invariants via operator-theoretic models.
motivation: To understand the structure and invariants of homogeneous submodules in the bidisc, which are of interest in operator theory and function spaces.
method: Uses weighted OPUC models, introducing Verblunsky coefficients to analyze wandering projections, core operators, and cross-commutators, along with Toeplitz-determinant and Mahler-measure identities.
result: Establishes exact Fredholm determinants, Schatten estimates, and asymptotic Hilbert-Schmidt norms, and provides a counterexample to proposed monotonicity of numerical invariants.
conclusion: The paper gives a comprehensive operator-theoretic characterization of these invariants, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Joint Beamforming And Phase Shifts Design For RIS-Enabled Rsma-isac Systems
authors: Xuejun Cheng, Qian Zhang, Yuhui Jiao, Yufei Zhao, Zheng Dong, Ju Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the sensing-centric design of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled rate-splitting multiple access-integrated sensing and communication (RSMA-ISAC) systems. Specifically, we propose a new beam-gain approximation method to enhance the sensing beam gain while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints.Since the joint optimization of the beamforming vectors and RIS phase shifts is highly coupled and non-convex, existing methods typically rely on generic optimization solvers involving substantial computational complexity. To address this issue, we propose an efficient constraints-separation-based alternating optimization algorithm (CS-AO). Our proposed algorithm effectively decouples the optimization variables and yields closed-form solutions for all subproblems, thereby significantly reducing the computational burden. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves sensing beam-gain performance comparable to successive convex approximation (SCA) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR) benchmarks, while achieving more than 120-fold and 50-fold runtime reductions. In addition, compared with conventional space-division multiple access (SDMA) schemes, the proposed design exhibits substantial sensing beam gain.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient alternating optimization algorithm for joint beamforming and phase shift design in RIS-enabled RSMA-ISAC systems to enhance sensing beam gain while meeting communication QoS.
motivation: The joint optimization problem is non-convex and computationally heavy; existing methods rely on generic solvers. The goal is to reduce computational complexity while maintaining performance.
method: A constraints-separation-based alternating optimization (CS-AO) algorithm is introduced, which decouples optimization variables and provides closed-form solutions for each subproblem, using a beam-gain approximation method.
result: Simulations show the algorithm achieves sensing beam-gain comparable to SCA and SDR benchmarks with over 120-fold and 50-fold runtime reductions, respectively, and outperforms SDMA.
conclusion: The proposed CS-AO algorithm offers a computationally efficient solution for RIS-enabled ISAC systems, balancing performance and complexity.

title: Sharp Sobolev Approximation On General Domains By Linearized Shallow Networks With Analytic Activations
authors: Jia Li, Tong Mao, Jinchao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Sobolev approximation on bounded domains by linearized shallow neural networks whose inner parameters are prescribed independently of the target function. Our main step is a one-dimensional construction for analytic activations. We prove that quasi-Chebyshev parameter sets with univariate resolution [MATH] generate fixed feature spaces attaining the sharp [MATH]-to-[MATH] approximation order [MATH] for a class of analytic activations satisfying a quantitative non-cancellation condition on their Taylor coefficients. Combining this result with the ridge-function lifting theorem in [SIAM J. Math. Anal. 30 (1998), pp. 155-189] and its extension to arbitrary quasi-uniform direction sets established in this work, we construct tensor-product-type parameter sets that attain the sharp rate $[MATH][MATH]r>0$. In contrast to the finite-difference construction in [Neural Comput. 8 (1996), pp. 164-177], whose explicit admissibility condition may require an extremely small parameter scale, the proposed parameter sets remain distributed over fixed intervals and are therefore more amenable to practical computation.
tldr: This paper proves sharp Sobolev approximation rates for linearized shallow neural networks with analytic activations using specifically constructed fixed parameter sets.
motivation: To achieve optimal approximation orders while keeping parameters fixed and computationally practical.
method: They use a one-dimensional construction, combine with a ridge-function lifting theorem, and extend to quasi-uniform direction sets to build tensor-product-type parameter sets.
result: They attain sharp approximation rates for a class of analytic activations, with parameters distributed over fixed intervals.
conclusion: Their parameter sets are more amenable to practical computation than previous finite-difference constructions.

title: Gcno: Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator For Physics-Based Compression Of Wireless Channels
authors: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Shahab Hamidi-Rad, Elahe Soltanaghai, Akshay Malhotra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large antenna arrays allow wireless systems to serve more users and achieve higher data rates, but they also make channel feedback expensive: the receiving device must repeatedly report a large complex-valued channel matrix to the base station. Most neural compressors treat this matrix like an image and replace it with a fixed-length code that only a matched neural decoder can interpret. The message therefore does not adapt to channel complexity, and changing the antenna count typically requires retraining. We ask whether a device can instead report only the few dominant propagation paths underlying each channel. We introduce the Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator (GCNO), a physics-based, variable-rate compressor that identifies a sample-dependent set of path directions. GCNO uses receive-transmit channel structure to locate paths, a first-order Taylor correction to refine directions that fall between grid points, and least squares to recover their complex strengths. It is trained without path labels, and the base station reconstructs the channel analytically from the transmitted path tuples rather than through a learned decoder. Across three ray-traced environments, GCNO achieves better reconstruction accuracy at the same payload - or lower payload at the same accuracy - than neural feedback baselines, and transfers to unseen antenna counts without retraining.
tldr: Presents a physics-based neural operator for variable-rate compression of wireless channels using dominant path extraction.
motivation: Large antenna arrays make channel feedback expensive; existing neural compressors have fixed-length codes and require retraining for different antenna counts.
method: Introduces Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator (GCNO) that identifies sample-dependent path directions using channel structure, Taylor correction for off-grid paths, and least squares for strengths, trained without path labels.
result: Achieves better reconstruction accuracy at same payload or lower payload at same accuracy than neural baselines across ray-traced environments, and transfers to unseen antenna counts.
conclusion: Demonstrates a physics-based, sample-dependent compression approach that adapts to channel complexity and generalizes across antenna configurations.

title: Constructing Good Abelian Codes Via Shift Bounds And Genetic Algorithms
authors: Cong Yu, Hao Chen, Zhonghua Sun, Shixin Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the construction of linear codes via abelian codes over finite fields. By exploiting the algebraic structure of multivariate polynomial quotient rings, we derive lower bounds on the minimum distance using a generalized shift bound, which extends the classical van Lint-Wilson bound for cyclic codes. Several infinite families of abelian codes are explicitly constructed, including binary and ternary cases that extend previously known cyclic constructions. To find more abelian codes with good parameters, we apply a genetic algorithm that searches over defining sets represented as binary chromosomes of cyclotomic cosets; the fitness function compares the computed minimum distance against the best known linear code (BKLC) bounds. The search yields multiple record-breaking codes over F_3 and F_4, with improvements over Grassl's tables. Furthermore, the nested structure of these codes enables the application of Construction X, yielding additional linear codes with improved parameters. The results demonstrate that abelian codes, combined with heuristic search, form a viable way for discovering linear codes with unknown parameters.
tldr: This paper constructs linear codes using abelian codes over finite fields, deriving shift bounds and employing genetic algorithms to find record-breaking codes.
motivation: To discover new linear codes with good parameters beyond existing cyclic constructions, leveraging the richer structure of abelian codes and heuristic search.
method: Exploits multivariate polynomial quotient rings to generalize the van Lint-Wilson shift bound for cyclic codes to abelian codes, explicitly constructs families, and uses a genetic algorithm over defining sets to search for codes with large minimum distance.
result: Yields multiple record-breaking codes over F_3 and F_4, improving on Grassl's tables, and applies Construction X to derive additional linear codes with improved parameters.
conclusion: Abelian codes combined with heuristic search are a viable approach for discovering linear codes with previously unknown parameters.

title: Long-run Risk-sensitive Portfolio Optimisation With Proportional Transaction Costs And Log L\'{e}vy Asset Prices
authors: \l{}ukasz Stettner Damian Jelito
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a long-run risk-sensitive portfolio problem with proportional transaction costs in a continuous-time market whose log-prices are given as a L\'{e}vy process, and rebalancing is possible only at random moments of investment opportunities. Using a Schauder fixed-point argument, we solve the ergodic Bellman equation without any mixing assumptions. Under additional full-support and growth conditions, the solution to the Bellman equation is unique, with the unique continuous maximiser. We also prove vanishing risk-aversion asymptotics towards the risk-neutral (Kelly) problem and convergence of a dyadic-time-grid approximation of the random intervention moments. Numerical examples illustrate the results.
tldr: This paper solves the ergodic Bellman equation for long-run risk-sensitive portfolio optimization with proportional transaction costs and Lévy price processes.
motivation: To address portfolio optimization in continuous time with transaction costs and random investment opportunities, which is a key problem in financial mathematics.
method: Uses a Schauder fixed-point argument to solve the Bellman equation, proves uniqueness under full-support and growth conditions, and derives vanishing risk-aversion asymptotics.
result: Establishes existence and uniqueness of the solution, convergence of a dyadic-time-grid approximation, and provides numerical examples.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous framework for long-run risk-sensitive portfolio optimization under realistic market conditions.

title: Xnet: Intelligent Dynamic Sampling For High-Speed Network Security Monitoring
authors: Thomas Papastergiou, Karthika Subramani, Joseph Reilly, Boladji Vinny Adjibi, Pierros-Christos Skafidas, Roberto Perdisci, Manos Antonakakis
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Growing network speeds, with 100GbE line rates becoming common in modern enterprise networks, pose challenges to operators and security applications, as they struggle to scale their operational efficiency accordingly, without relying on costly hardware, excessive sampling, or complex distributed deployments. Unintentional loss due to stochastic packet sampling often produces low-quality traffic, further risking missed detection of critical security incidents, particularly those hidden in typically low-rate traffic, such as APT/malware command-and-control communications. In this paper, we introduce XNET, a system that monitors traffic at line rate using commodity hardware and applies dynamic sampling to amplify the visibility of high security value traffic. XNET leverages Linux's XDP technology to process packets efficiently, classify them based on their security value, and sample them as per configured policies. The outcome is a reduced packet stream in which the security-relevant portion of the traffic is amplified at the expense of less interesting traffic segments. XNET is a highly flexible, scalable and dynamic system that can be adapted based on a network's needs. We deployed XNET in a large real-world network using only commodity hardware, where our results show that XNET can achieve up to 84% traffic reduction with no packet loss while increasing the visibility of otherwise negligible traffic fivefold. With controlled stress tests, we further demonstrate XNET's scalability up to 100Gbps. Additionally, we show that XNET sampling led to a detection rate of 99.6% in an IDS application.
tldr: Introduces XNET, a network security monitoring system using dynamic sampling based on security value to handle high-speed traffic.
motivation: High-speed networks cause packet loss and missed security events, especially for low-rate traffic like APT communications.
method: XNET uses Linux XDP to process packets at line rate, classify them by security value, and sample accordingly to amplify important traffic.
result: Achieves up to 84% traffic reduction with no loss, fivefold visibility increase for low-rate traffic, and 99.6% detection rate in IDS application, scaling to 100Gbps.
conclusion: Offers an efficient, scalable solution for network security monitoring on commodity hardware.

title: Beyond Distortion Robustness: Rethinking Severe Cropping As Erasure-Resilient Message Embedding
authors: Bo Pang, Weibin Kong, Juntu Dong, Minghan Li, Zhongping Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust message embedding in images is important for multimedia security applications such as copyright protection and content tracing. Existing methods are largely developed under a distortion robustness paradigm, where the embedded signal remains spatially present but is degraded by noise, blur, or compression. Severe cropping poses a fundamentally different challenge because it removes part of the carrier itself, causing partial payload disappearance rather than mere signal corruption. In this paper, we revisit robust message embedding from an erasure-resilience perspective and present CREST, a proof-of-concept framework for severe-cropping-robust embedding. CREST combines coding-theoretic redundancy with neural embedding and recovery by expanding a compact QR message into a redundant spatial payload via LT fountain coding and coupling it with cropping-aware embedding and fragment recovery. Experiments on COCO, DIV2K, and VOC2012 show that CREST improves recovery under severe cropping while maintaining competitive visual quality. Under mixed distortions with an area retention ratio of 0.7, CREST improves TRA from 18.52% to 68.45% and reduces EMR from 13.88% to 4.21% over the strongest baseline. On COCO2017, CREST still achieves 48.55--65.12% TRA when only 30--50% of the image area is retained, whereas all compared baselines fail to recover the message. These results suggest that severe cropping is better understood as an erasure problem rather than a conventional distortion problem, motivating the joint design of neural embedding and coding-based recovery.
tldr: CREST uses fountain coding and neural embedding to make message embedding robust to severe cropping by treating it as an erasure problem.
motivation: Existing robust embedding methods fail under severe cropping because they treat it as distortion, but cropping removes part of the carrier, causing message erasure.
method: CREST expands a compact QR message into a redundant spatial payload via LT fountain coding and couples it with cropping-aware embedding and fragment recovery.
result: Experiments show CREST significantly improves recovery metrics under severe cropping, e.g., TRA from 18.52% to 68.45% at 0.7 retention ratio, while maintaining competitive visual quality.
conclusion: Severe cropping is better understood as an erasure problem, and jointly designing neural embedding with coding-based recovery improves robustness.

title: Monad Structures On Topological Spaces Comprising Mislove's Random Variables
authors: Qingguo Li Chengyu Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mislove, Goubault and Varacca investigated how to define random variables in Domain theory to form monads over the category of bounded complete domains. They intended to model probabilistic programming languages with their random variables monads. In this paper, we focus on the random variables defined by Mislove from a topological perspective. We provide a topology for [MATH]-max continuous random variables on a [MATH] space, we construct a new [MATH] space, where [MATH]-max property is essential for the monad structures. We show that the spaces of normalized [MATH]-max simple random variables form a monad over the category of [MATH] spaces and that the spaces of normalized [MATH]-max continuous random variables give a monad over the category of d-spaces. In addition, on a sober space, the space of normalized [MATH]-max continuous random variables is the sobrification of the space of normalized [MATH]-max simple random variables.
tldr: This paper investigates monad structures on topological spaces built from Mislove's random variables, extending domain-theoretic probabilistic semantics to a topological setting.
motivation: Mislove et al. defined random variables as monads over bounded complete domains to model probabilistic programming; this work aims to provide a topological perspective and construct monads on spaces of random variables.
method: The authors define a topology on spaces of max-continuous random variables, construct new spaces based on the max-property, and prove that normalized max-simple and max-continuous random variables form monads over categories of spaces and d-spaces respectively.
result: It is shown that normalized max-simple random variables form a monad over [MATH] spaces, and normalized max-continuous random variables form a monad over d-spaces; also, the latter is the sobrification of the former on sober spaces.
